definition_zh: 时期；阶段；周期；课时；句号；经期
definition_en: a length of time, a stage in history or a process, a recurring cycle, a lesson, or the full stop at the end of a sentence
core_image: 一条走了一圈又回到原点的轨道：起点与终点重合，中间那段就是一圈。
scene: The Victorian period saw the first underground railways in the world.
sceneCN: 这里 period 是「历史上的一段时期」（第 2 个义项：时代、阶段）；句意：维多利亚时期出现了世界上最早的地下铁路。场景要点：煤气灯、砖砌车站、旧式火车。

pos.zh: 时期；阶段；周期；课时；句号；经期
某一时代的；仿古的（如 period furniture）

collocations.zh: 时代风格的作品；古装作品

senses.title: A length of time with limits
senses.titleCN: 一段时间：有头有尾
senses.definition: a length of time during which something happens, especially one with a clear beginning and end
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生所经历的一段时间，尤指有明确起止的
senses.example: The study covered a period of five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究覆盖了五年时间。
senses.why: Greek periodos was 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. A measured stretch of time is a closed loop with a start and a finish.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 periodos 是“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。被量出的一段时光，就是一个有起点和终点的闭环。

senses.title: A stage of history
senses.titleCN: 时代：历史的一章
senses.definition: a particular stretch of history with its own character, style, or events
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身特征、风格或事件的历史阶段
senses.example: The country changed its alphabet twice in that period.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在那个时期两次更换文字。
senses.why: History is cut into loops: a culture goes through a way of doing things and comes out the other side, leaving a named stretch behind.
senses.whyCN: 历史被切成一圈一圈：一种文化走完一套做法，从另一边出来，留下一段被命名的时光。

senses.title: A recurring cycle
senses.titleCN: 周期：又一次转回来
senses.definition: a regular interval after which an event or process repeats
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件或过程重复出现所间隔的固定时间
senses.example: The comet returns every 76 years, its orbital period.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗彗星每 76 年回归一次，这就是它的轨道周期。
senses.why: This is the most literal sense: a body goes around and comes back to the same place. The interval is the time the loop takes.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：一个物体绕行一圈，回到同一位置。这个间隔就是那一圈所花的时间。

senses.title: One lesson in a school day
senses.titleCN: 课时：课表上的一格
senses.definition: one of the fixed blocks of time into which a school day is divided
senses.definitionCN: 学校一天被划分成的若干个固定时间段之一
senses.example: We have two periods of chemistry on Tuesdays.
senses.exampleCN: 我们周二有两节化学课。
senses.why: The school day is cut into loops of equal length. Each block is a period because it is a closed, measured unit that ends when the bell rings.
senses.whyCN: 学校的一天被切成等长的圈。每一格都是 period，因为它是一个封闭的、被量出的单位，铃响就结束。

senses.title: The full stop in punctuation
senses.titleCN: 句号：让一句话收口
senses.definition: the mark at the end of a declarative sentence
senses.definitionCN: 陈述句末尾的那个标点
senses.example: Delete the extra period at the end of the citation.
senses.exampleCN: 删掉引文末尾多余的那个句号。
senses.why: Recorded from the 1580s. A sentence is a loop of thought; the full stop closes the loop, which is why the mark took the name of a completed cycle.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。一个句子是一圈思想；句号把这一圈合上，所以这个符号借用了“完成一个周期”的名字。

senses.title: Menstruation
senses.titleCN: 经期：按月转回的那几天
senses.definition: the monthly bleeding cycle in a person who menstruates, or the time it lasts
senses.definitionCN: 有月经的人每月一次的出血周期，或该周期持续的几天
senses.example: The app tracks the length of each period.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用记录每次经期的长度。
senses.why: Recorded from 1822. The bodily cycle returns at a regular interval, so the medical use simply names the most visible human example of a period.
senses.whyCN: 1822 年见于记录。身体周期按固定间隔转回来，医学用法只是把人类最可见的一个“周期”例子叫成了 period。

senses.title: One division of a sports game
senses.titleCN: 比赛分节：把一场球切成几段
senses.definition: one of the equal parts into which a game such as ice hockey is divided
senses.definitionCN: 冰球等比赛中把整场划分成的若干个等长时间段之一
senses.example: They scored twice in the second period.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在第二节里进了两球。
senses.why: A game is another closed stretch of time divided into loops. Each period starts with a face-off and ends with a whistle.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛也是一段被切成若干圈的封闭时间。每一节从开球开始，到哨响结束。

senses.title: Belonging to a past style
senses.titleCN: 仿古的：带着某个时代的样子
senses.definition: of furniture, costume, or a work, made in or imitating the style of a particular historical period
senses.definitionCN: 指家具、服装或作品按某一历史时期的风格制作或仿制
senses.example: The room was furnished with period pieces from the 1780s.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆着 1780 年代的仿古家具。
senses.why: The noun becomes an adjective: an object carries the look of a named loop of history, so it is 'period' rather than merely old.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为形容词：一件物品带着某段被命名的历史圈的样子，所以它是“时期的”，而不只是“旧的”。

intro.en: Period is Greek periodos 'a going around', from peri 'around' + hodos 'way'. English borrowed it through Latin and first used it for a cycle of time.
intro.cn: period 是希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”构成。英语经拉丁语借入，最早用来指时间的循环。

items.en: Hodos meant 'way, road, journey'. It survives in English compounds such as method ('a way along') and period.
items.cn: hodos 意为“路、道路、行程”。它保留在英语的 method（“沿路而行”）与 period 等复合词里。

items.en: Periodos meant 'a going around, a circuit, a cycle', used of the sun's course and of rhetorical sentences that round off.
items.cn: periodos 意为“绕行、一圈、循环”，用于太阳的运行，也用于首尾完整、能收口的修辞句子。

items.en: Latin took periodus as a term of astronomy and rhetoric. Its sense of a rounded sentence is why the closing mark later took this name.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 periodus 作为天文学与修辞学术语使用。它“首尾完整的句子”这一义，正是后来收尾标点取这个名字的原因。

items.en: English records period around 1400 meaning 'course, extent of time, cycle'. The historical sense 'a named age' develops from this.
items.cn: 英语在 1400 年前后记录 period，意为“进程、时间长度、周期”。历史的“被命名的时代”义由此发展而来。

items.en: The punctuation sense is recorded in the 1580s. A full stop is literally the mark that closes the period of a sentence.
items.cn: 标点义于 16 世纪 80 年代见于记录。句号字面上就是“合上一句话的那一圈”的记号。

items.en: The menstrual sense is recorded from 1822, and the school and sports senses follow the same model: a day or a game cut into closed blocks of time.
items.cn: 经期义于 1822 年见于记录；课时与比赛分节义遵循同样的模式：把一天或一场比赛切成封闭的时间块。

note.en: The first group is the period family plus compounds built on it; the second collects words for stretches of time.
note.cn: 第一组是 period 词族及由它构成的复合词；第二组收“时间段”类近义词。

entries.definition: happening at regular intervals, or relating to a period. It is the adjective of period, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的。它是 period 的形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: a magazine published at regular intervals, or published regularly. The noun sense is a publication, not a time span.
entries.definitionCN: 定期出版的杂志；定期出版的。名词指出版物，不是时间段。

entries.definition: an object or work valued for its style from a past era. Here period works as an adjective meaning 'of a historical era'.
entries.definitionCN: 因带有过去时代风格而有价值的物品或作品。这里 period 作形容词，意为“某一历史时代的”。

entries.definition: the quality of occurring in regular cycles. It names the abstract property behind periodic.
entries.definitionCN: 按规律周期发生的性质。它命名 periodic 背后的抽象属性。

entries.definition: a long period of history named after a system, leader, or event. It is usually larger and more formal than period.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种制度、领袖或事件命名的长历史阶段。它通常比 period 更大、更正式。

entries.definition: a period that begins with a striking change and is treated as a new starting point. It stresses the break, not just the length.
entries.definitionCN: 以显著变化开始、被视为新起点的时期。它强调断裂，而不只是长度。

entries.definition: a long stretch of history associated with a way of life, as in the Bronze Age or the age of the internet. It is looser than period.
entries.definitionCN: 与某种生活方式相关联的长历史阶段，如青铜时代、互联网时代。它比 period 宽松。

entries.definition: a fixed length of time for which something lasts, such as a school term or a prison term. It is defined by an agreement or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的固定时长，如学期、刑期。它由约定或规则界定。

entries.definition: a short period of a particular activity or weather. It is informal and almost always short.
entries.definitionCN: 某活动或天气的一小段。它口语化，且几乎总是很短。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek peri 'around' + hodos 'way', giving periodos 'a going around'. Family words periodic, periodical, periodically, periodicity, and compounds period piece and grace period.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路”，合成 periodos“绕行一周”。词族为 periodic、periodical、periodically、periodicity，以及复合词 period piece、grace period。

normal.en: Period and method share hodos 'way': one is a way around, the other a way along.
normal.cn: period 与 method 共享 hodos“路”：一个是绕一圈的路，一个是沿着走的路。

normal.en: A full stop is called a period because it closes the sentence's circuit.
normal.cn: 句号叫 period，是因为它把句子的回路合上。

normal.en: A school day is cut into periods the way a circle is cut into arcs.
normal.cn: 学校的一天被切成 period，就像圆被切成弧。

normal.en: Periodic table: elements arranged by repeating cycles of properties.
normal.cn: 元素周期表：按性质重复的周期排列元素。

normal.en: A period piece is an object still wearing the clothes of its era.
normal.cn: period piece 是一件还穿着它那个时代衣服的物品。

abstract.en: History is only manageable because we agree to cut it into loops.
abstract.cn: 历史之所以可处理，只是因为我们同意把它切成一圈一圈。

abstract.en: A period is a promise that the sentence will end.
abstract.cn: 句号是一个承诺：这句话会结束。

abstract.en: Every cycle is a way of saying that the same place can be reached again.
abstract.cn: 每一个周期，都是在说同一个地方还能再被抵达。

examples.en: Sales rose sharply over the same period last year.
examples.cn: 销售额在去年同期那段时期大幅上升。

examples.en: The teacher gave us ten minutes at the end of the period.
examples.cn: 老师在那一节课末尾给了我们十分钟。

examples.en: Put a period at the end of every complete sentence.
examples.cn: 每个完整的句子末尾都要加句号。

dict_mnemonic.text: “皮瑞尔的”——皮瑞尔的怀表每绕一圈就响一次，一圈就是一段 → period 周期、时期

root: 源自希腊语 periodos“绕行一周”，由 peri“环绕”+ hodos“路、行程”构成；经拉丁语 periodus、古法语进入英语，约 1400 年义为“进程、时长、周期”。核心是“绕一圈所花的那段时间”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of period, all one shape: a closed stretch that begins, runs its course, and comes back to an end.
sensesIntro.cn: period 的八个义项是同一个形状：一段封闭的时间，开始、走完、回到终点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track that leaves a point, goes all the way around, and returns to the same point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从某点出发、绕行一圈、又回到同一点的轨道。

branches.en: SPAN: from a five-year study to the Victorian age, every span is a loop someone has marked off.
branches.cn: 跨度：从五年的研究到维多利亚时代，每一段都是有人划出的一圈。

branches.en: REPETITION: an orbit and a hockey game both return to the start on a schedule.
branches.cn: 重复：轨道与冰球比赛，都按时刻表回到起点。

branches.en: BODY AND SCHOOL: the timetable and the monthly cycle are the same closed block imposed on living time.
branches.cn: 身体与学校：课表与月度周期，都是加在活的时间上的同一种封闭块。

branches.en: PUNCTUATION: the mark that closes a sentence borrows the name of a completed circuit.
branches.cn: 标点：合上句子的符号，借用了“完成一圈”的名字。

branches.en: STYLE: an object can still carry the look of the loop it was made in.
branches.cn: 风格：一件物品仍然带着它被造出时那一圈的样子。

intro.en: Period's family is built on the Greek compound periodos. Suffixes turn it into an adjective, an adverb, and a noun of property; compounds name the things people measure in cycles.
intro.cn: period 的词族建立在希腊复合词 periodos 上。后缀把它变成形容词、副词与属性名词；复合词则命名人们按周期计量的东西。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are Greek hodos 'way', periodos 'circuit', and Latin periodus, the borrowing English received. Latin added no new root.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是希腊语 hodos“路”、periodos“一圈”与拉丁语借形 periodus，英语承接的正是后者。拉丁语没有新增词根。

items.meaning: occurring at regular intervals; relating to a period
items.meaningCN: 按固定间隔发生的；与周期有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The system runs a periodic backup every night.
items.exampleCN: 系统每晚执行一次定期备份。

items.meaning: published at regular intervals; a magazine so published
items.meaningCN: 定期出版的；定期刊物（-al 构成形容词，也可作名词）
items.example: The library keeps back issues of the periodical.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆保存这份期刊的过刊。

items.meaningCN: 定期地；周期性地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: the quality of recurring in cycles
items.meaningCN: 按周期重复的性质（-ity 构成属性名词）
items.example: The periodicity of the signal suggests a rotating source.
items.exampleCN: 信号的周期性表明源头在旋转。

items.meaning: a work or object valued for its historical style
items.meaningCN: 因历史风格而有价值的作品或物品
items.example: The film is a period piece set in 1912.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影是设定在 1912 年的年代戏。

items.meaning: extra time allowed before a penalty applies
items.meaningCN: 在处罚生效前额外允许的时间
items.example: The bank offers a ten-day grace period.

items.meaning: a particular stretch of time being discussed
items.meaningCN: 正在讨论的某一特定时间段
items.example: Over this time period, prices doubled.
items.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，价格上涨了一倍。

items.example: She takes two days off for period pain each month.
items.exampleCN: 她每月因经期疼痛休息两天。

items.meaning: the arrangement of elements by repeating chemical properties
items.meaningCN: 按化学性质重复规律排列元素的表格
items.example: Carbon sits in the second row of the periodic table.
items.exampleCN: 碳位于元素周期表第二行。

items.meaning: clothing made in the style of a historical era
items.meaningCN: 按历史时期风格制作的服装
items.example: The actors wore period costume in every scene.
items.exampleCN: 演员在每一场都穿年代服装。

latinEntries.meaning: a circuit; a complete sentence; a cycle of time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一圈；完整的句子；时间周期

definition_zh: 坚持；持续；执意；存留；持久化
definition_en: to keep doing something despite difficulty, or to continue to exist beyond the expected time
core_image: 一个人站在原地不动，风一直吹，他始终没退一步。
scene: The cough persisted for three weeks after the fever cleared.
sceneCN: 这里 persist 是「（症状）持续不退」（第 3 个义项：病症延续）；句意：退烧之后，咳嗽还持续了三周。场景要点：药瓶、日历上划掉的日期、仍在咳的人。

derivatives.zh: 坚持不懈的；持续的；顽固的
非持久的（多用于计算机或化学语境）

senses.title: Keep going despite difficulty
senses.titleCN: 坚持不懈：难也不退
senses.definition: to continue an effort even when it is hard or slow to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 即使困难或见效缓慢，仍继续努力
senses.example: She persisted with the experiment after four failed trials.
senses.exampleCN: 四次试验失败后，她仍坚持做这个实验。
senses.why: Latin sistere meant 'to stand firm, take a stand'. Persist is per- 'thoroughly' + sistere: to stand your ground all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sistere 意为“站稳、站定”。persist 是 per-“彻底”+ sistere：从头到尾站住不退。

senses.title: Continue to exist
senses.titleCN: 持续存在：没有消失
senses.definition: of a condition, practice, or thing, to continue to exist over time
senses.definitionCN: 指某种状况、做法或事物随时间继续存在
senses.example: The custom persists in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在农村地区仍然存在。
senses.why: The standing image is applied to existence itself: something that stands does not fall away, so it keeps being there.
senses.whyCN: “站住”的意象被用在存在本身：站住的东西不会倒掉，因此一直还在。

senses.title: Of a symptom: fail to clear
senses.titleCN: 病症不退：拖着不走
senses.definition: of an illness or symptom, to continue longer than expected
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或症状持续的时间超过预期
senses.example: See a doctor if the fever persists for more than three days.
senses.exampleCN: 如果发烧持续超过三天，请就医。
senses.why: A symptom is something standing in the body that refuses to leave. The verb marks duration, not effort, which is why medical usage is so common.
senses.whyCN: 症状是站在身体里不肯走的东西。这个动词标记的是“时程”而非“努力”，所以医学用法很常见。

senses.title: Of a smell or trace: remain
senses.titleCN: 气味留存：散不掉
senses.definition: of a smell, taste, impression, or mark, to remain after its source has gone
senses.definitionCN: 指气味、味道、印象或痕迹在来源消失后仍然留着
senses.example: The smell of smoke persisted in the curtains for days.
senses.exampleCN: 烟味在窗帘上留了好几天。
senses.why: The trace keeps standing in the material even after the fire is out. Persistence here is physical stubbornness.
senses.whyCN: 火灭了，痕迹仍站在布料里。这里的持续，是一种物理上的不肯走。

senses.title: Keep asking or doing, annoyingly
senses.titleCN: 执意纠缠：一遍遍不放
senses.definition: to continue doing or asking something in a way that others find hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 以别人难以阻止的方式反复做或反复问
senses.example: He persisted in calling until she answered.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直打个不停，直到她接电话。
senses.why: The same standing firm can be read from outside as refusal to take no for an answer. The virtue turns into a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“站住”，从外面看就是不肯接受“不”。美德由此变成了烦扰。

senses.title: Of a belief or institution: survive
senses.titleCN: 观念延续：穿过年代还在
senses.definition: of a belief, institution, or idea, to survive over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 指信念、制度或观念长期存续下来
senses.example: The belief persisted long after the empire fell.
senses.exampleCN: 帝国灭亡很久之后，这种信仰仍然延续。
senses.why: Institutions stand longer than the people who hold them up. Persistence becomes a measure of historical survival.
senses.whyCN: 制度比撑着它的人站得更久。持续由此成为衡量历史存活的尺度。

senses.title: Computing: store data permanently
senses.titleCN: 持久化：断电也还在
senses.definition: of data, to remain stored after a program or device stops running
senses.definitionCN: 指数据在程序或设备停止运行后仍然保留
senses.example: The settings persist even after a restart.
senses.exampleCN: 即使重启，设置也会保留。
senses.why: Memory that vanishes is data that could not stand. Persistent storage is the technical version of 'still standing after the power goes off'.
senses.whyCN: 一断电就消失的记忆，是站不住的数据。持久化存储，就是“断电后仍站着”的技术版本。

senses.title: Insist stubbornly against advice
senses.titleCN: 固执坚持：不听劝
senses.definition: to continue in a course of action in spite of warnings or good advice
senses.definitionCN: 不顾警告或善意劝告，继续照自己的做法行事
senses.example: He persisted in driving despite the closed-road signs.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有封路标志，他仍执意开车。
senses.why: Standing firm with no reason to stand is stubbornness. The word does not judge by itself; the context decides whether to praise or blame.
senses.whyCN: 没有理由还站着，就是固执。这个词本身不作评判，是语境决定该夸还是该责。

intro.en: Persist is Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'to stand firm', from the same Indo-European root as stand. The core is not effort but posture: staying on your feet.
intro.cn: persist 是拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，与 stand 同出一个印欧词根。它的核心不是努力，而是姿态：站住不倒。

items.en: The root *sta- gives Latin stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and English stand, stable, statue, and constant.
items.cn: 词根 *sta- 衍生出拉丁语 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”，以及英语 stand、stable、statue、constant。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, place, stop'. Its frequentative form was used for holding a position, which is the seed of 'persist'.
items.cn: sistere 意为“使站住、安置、停住”。它的反复形式用于“守住位置”，这正是 persist 的种子。

items.en: Persistere combined per- 'through, thoroughly' with sistere: 'to continue standing, persevere, persist'.
items.cn: persistere 把 per-“贯穿、彻底”与 sistere 结合：“一直站住、坚持、持续”。

items.en: English records persist in the 1530s, first of persons continuing in a course, then of things continuing to exist.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 30 年代记录 persist，先指人继续走某条路，后指事物继续存在。

items.en: The medical sense of a symptom that will not clear and the physical sense of a smell that remains both grow from the same 'still standing' image.
items.cn: 症状不退的医学义与气味残留的物理义，都从同一个“仍站着”的意象长出来。

items.en: Persistent storage and persistent data apply the old verb to memory that survives a restart. Persistence becomes a technical property.
items.cn: persistent storage 与 persistent data 把这个老动词用在重启后仍存活的内存上。持续由此成为一种技术属性。

note.en: The first group is the persist family plus the Latin verb behind it; the second separates near-synonyms by what exactly keeps going.
note.cn: 第一组是 persist 词族及其背后的拉丁动词；第二组按“究竟是什么在继续”区分近义词。

entries.definition: the quality of continuing despite difficulty, or of lasting. It is the noun of persist.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续的品质，或持久性。它是 persist 的名词。

entries.definition: continuing firmly or lasting a long time. It describes the person or thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的。它描述人或物，而非动作。

entries.definition: a rarer synonym of persistence, used especially in older technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: persistence 的较罕见同义词，多用于较早的技术文献。

entries.definition: not lasting, used of chemicals that break down quickly and of network connections that close after use.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的，用于快速降解的化学品，或用完即关闭的网络连接。

entries.definition: to keep trying despite difficulty. It is close to persist but almost always about deliberate human effort toward a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍不断尝试。它与 persist 接近，但几乎总指人为目标付出的努力。

entries.definition: to keep happening or doing without stopping. It is the neutral word and carries no idea of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 不停地继续发生或做。它最中性，不含抵抗之意。

entries.definition: to suffer something difficult patiently, or to last a long time. It adds the weight of suffering or durability.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心承受艰难，或长久存在。它加了受苦或耐久的分量。

entries.definition: to stay longer than expected, often unwillingly. It is used of smells, illness, and people who should go.
entries.definitionCN: 比预期停留更久，常含不愿离开。它用于气味、疾病与该走的人。

entries.definition: to demand something firmly. It is about a claim or demand, while persist is about continuing an action.
entries.definitionCN: 坚决要求。它关于主张或要求，而 persist 关于继续行动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand firm', from PIE *sta- 'stand'. Family words persistence, persistent, persistently; relatives stand, stable, statue, constant.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，源自原始印欧语 *sta-“站”。词族为 persistence、persistent、persistently；亲属词 stand、stable、statue、constant。

normal.en: Sistere is 'stand firm'; persist is standing firm all the way through.
normal.cn: sistere 是“站稳”；persist 就是从头到尾一直站稳。

normal.en: Stand, stable, statue, constant, persist: one *sta- family of standing.
normal.cn: stand、stable、statue、constant、persist：同一个 *sta-“站立”家族。

normal.en: A persistent cough is a cough that will not stand down.
normal.cn: persistent cough 就是不肯“退下”的咳嗽。

normal.en: Persistent data is data still standing after the power is cut.
normal.cn: persistent data 就是断电后仍站着的数据。

normal.en: Persist in and persist with are both about refusing to leave the spot.
normal.cn: persist in 与 persist with，都是不肯离开那个位置。

abstract.en: Persistence is often just the decision to remain where the difficulty is.
abstract.cn: 坚持，常常只是决定留在困难所在的那个地方。

abstract.en: What persists shapes the world more than what is intense.
abstract.cn: 留下来的东西，比强烈的东西更能塑造世界。

abstract.en: To persist is to make time your ally rather than your judge.
abstract.cn: 坚持，就是把时间变成盟友，而不是法官。

examples.en: The team persisted through two years of rejected applications.
examples.cn: 团队在两年申请被拒的情况下仍坚持下来。

examples.en: Old farming methods persist in the valley.
examples.cn: 古老的耕作方式在山谷里仍然延续。

examples.en: The rash persisted after the course of antibiotics ended.
examples.cn: 抗生素疗程结束后，皮疹仍未消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破吸石”——破吸盘还能吸在石头上不掉，风再大也不松 → persist 坚持、持续

root: 源自拉丁语 persistere“一直站住、坚持”，由 per-“贯穿、彻底”+ sistere“站稳、使站住”构成；sistere 与 stare“站”同出原始印欧语 *sta-“站”，故与 stand、stable、statue、constant 同源。核心是“站住不倒”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of persist, all one posture: something stays standing when it could have fallen, stopped, or gone away.
sensesIntro.cn: persist 的八个义项是同一个姿态：本可以倒下、停止或离开的东西，仍然站着。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in wind, feet planted, not moving back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在风里，双脚钉住，不退一步。

branches.en: WILL: effort and stubbornness are the same posture seen from inside and from outside.
branches.cn: 意志：努力与固执，是同一个姿态从里面和外面看的样子。

branches.en: EXISTENCE: a custom or belief stands longer than the people holding it up.
branches.cn: 存在：习俗或信仰，比撑着它的人站得更久。

branches.en: TRACES: a symptom and a smell both stay in the body or the cloth after their cause is gone.
branches.cn: 痕迹：症状与气味，都在成因消失后仍留在身体或布料里。

branches.en: PRESSURE: asking again and again is standing firm in someone else's doorway.
branches.cn: 压力：一遍遍追问，就是在别人的门口站住不走。

branches.en: MACHINES: persistent storage is memory that survives the power being switched off.
branches.cn: 机器：持久化存储，是断电后仍存活的内存。

intro.en: Persist's family is built on Latin sistere 'to stand firm'. Suffixes mark the state, the person or thing, and the manner; non- removes the lasting.
intro.cn: persist 的词族建立在拉丁语 sistere“站稳”上。后缀标记状态、人与方式；non- 则取消“持久”。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and persistere 'continue standing'. The whole family belongs to PIE *sta-.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”与 persistere“继续站住”。整个词族都属于原始印欧语 *sta-。

items.meaning: the fact or quality of continuing or lasting
items.meaningCN: 继续或持久的事实或品质（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Her persistence eventually won the funding.
items.exampleCN: 她的坚持最终争取到了资助。

items.meaning: continuing firmly or lasting a long time
items.meaningCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 持续不断的雨取消了比赛。

items.meaning: in a continuing or stubborn manner
items.meaningCN: 持续地；固执地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a rarer form of persistence, chiefly technical
items.meaningCN: persistence 的较罕见形式，主要用于技术文献
items.example: The persistency of the pesticide was measured in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种农药在土壤中的持久性被测定了。

items.meaning: not lasting long in the environment or in memory
items.meaningCN: 在环境中或内存中不长久留存的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: Non-persistent chemicals break down within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性化学品在几周内降解。

items.meaning: to continue doing something, often against advice
items.meaningCN: 继续做某事，常指不听劝（in 标记活动）
items.example: They persisted in asking for a written answer.
items.exampleCN: 他们执意要求一份书面答复。

items.meaning: to continue with a task or plan
items.meaningCN: 继续某项工作或计划（with 标记对象）
items.example: She persisted with the treatment for a full year.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持治疗了整整一年。

items.meaning: a person who keeps committing offences
items.meaningCN: 反复犯罪的人（法律术语）
items.example: He was classified as a persistent offender.

items.meaning: memory that keeps data after power is removed
items.meaningCN: 断电后仍保存数据的存储（计算机术语）
items.example: The logs are written to persistent storage.
items.exampleCN: 日志被写入持久化存储。

items.meaning: the way an image stays on the retina briefly and makes film appear to move
items.meaningCN: 图像在视网膜上短暂停留、使电影看起来在动的现象
items.example: Animation relies on the persistence of vision.

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, place, stop

definition_zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景
definition_en: a particular way of seeing or thinking about something, the art of showing depth on a flat surface, or the ability to judge things in proportion
core_image: 站在一个固定的位置透过窗框看出去：位置一换，看到的东西就重排。
scene: From the perspective of a farmer, the drought is a disaster; from the reservoir's, it is a reprieve.
sceneCN: 这里 perspective 是「看问题的角度」（第 1 个义项：视角、观点）；句意：从农民的角度看，这场干旱是灾难；从水库的角度看，却是喘息之机。场景要点：干裂的田、下降的水位标尺。

pos.zh: 观点；视角；透视法；洞察力；远景

collocations.zh: 正确看待某事；把某事放到应有的比例中

senses.title: A point of view
senses.titleCN: 视角：从哪个位置看
senses.definition: a particular way of looking at or thinking about something, shaped by where you stand
senses.definitionCN: 由于所处位置而形成的看或思考某事的特定方式
senses.example: The novel tells the same event from three perspectives.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说从三个视角讲述同一件事。
senses.why: Latin perspicere meant 'to look through'. Perspective is the view you get from one position, as if looking through a particular opening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 perspicere 意为“看穿、看透”。perspective 就是从某一个位置透过特定开口所得到的视野。

senses.title: The ability to judge proportion
senses.titleCN: 分寸感：知道什么更重要
senses.definition: the ability to see how important things really are in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间真实轻重关系的能力
senses.example: Losing one game gave the team a sense of perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉一场比赛反而让球队有了分寸感。
senses.why: Depth in a drawing comes from things being the right size relative to distance. Judging importance is the same skill applied to life.
senses.whyCN: 画面中的纵深，来自物体相对于距离的正确大小。判断重要性，是把同一种本事用在生活上。

senses.title: Art: the geometry of depth
senses.titleCN: 透视法：让平面显出纵深
senses.definition: the technique of representing three-dimensional space and depth on a flat surface
senses.definitionCN: 在平面上表现三维空间与纵深的技法
senses.example: The fresco uses linear perspective to draw the eye down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画用线性透视把视线引向走廊深处。
senses.why: Renaissance painters formalized the idea that parallel lines converge to a vanishing point. Seeing 'through' the canvas is the literal source.
senses.whyCN: 文艺复兴画家把“平行线汇聚于消失点”形式化。透过画布“看进去”，正是这个词的字面来源。

senses.title: A distant view
senses.titleCN: 远景：望出去的那一片
senses.definition: a view, especially a wide or distant one, seen from a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 从某一地点看到的景色，尤指开阔或辽远的
senses.example: The ridge offers a perspective of the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊上能看到整个山谷的远景。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense in English: what is seen from here, extending away from the viewer.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最古老的物理义：从这里看出去、向远处铺开的东西。

senses.title: A considered opinion on a matter
senses.titleCN: 看法：经过思量的立场
senses.definition: a considered attitude or evaluation of a subject, often one among several
senses.definitionCN: 对某主题经过思考的态度或评价，常为多种之一
senses.example: We need the perspective of someone outside the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一位行业外人士的看法。
senses.why: The visual metaphor becomes argumentative: a standpoint is a place you stand, and what you see from there is your opinion.
senses.whyCN: 视觉比喻变成论辩性的：立场就是你站的地方，从那里看到的东西就是你的观点。

senses.title: Psychology: taking another's viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 换位思考：站到别人的位置
senses.definition: in psychology, the capacity to understand another person's point of view
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中理解他人视角的能力
senses.example: Perspective-taking improves negotiation outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 换位思考能改善谈判结果。
senses.why: The word is used literally here: you imagine standing where the other stands, and the scene rearranges itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里用的是字面义：你想象站到对方所站的位置，整个场景就重新排列了。

senses.title: Proportion restored: in perspective
senses.titleCN: 比例复原：把事放回它的尺寸
senses.definition: in the phrase in perspective, shown at its true relative size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in perspective，表示按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
senses.example: The loss looks small when seen in perspective.
senses.exampleCN: 从整体比例看，这点损失显得很小。
senses.why: In a correct drawing, near things are large and far things small. Seeing something 'in perspective' is seeing it at the size its distance deserves.
senses.whyCN: 在正确的画里，近的大、远的小。把某事“in perspective”看，就是按它的距离应得的大小去看。

senses.title: Geometry: projection from a viewpoint
senses.titleCN: 投影法：从视点投出去的几何
senses.definition: in geometry, the system that projects a scene onto a plane from a chosen point
senses.definitionCN: 几何中从选定视点把场景投射到平面上的体系
senses.example: Perspective projection distorts parallel lines, unlike orthographic projection.
senses.exampleCN: 与正交投影不同，透视投影会使平行线产生畸变。
senses.why: The artistic technique becomes a mathematical one: a chosen eye point and a plane, with straight lines from one to the other.
senses.whyCN: 艺术技法变成了数学体系：一个选定的眼点、一个平面，以及从一点到另一点的直线。

intro.en: Perspective is Latin perspicere 'to look through' turned into a noun. English first used it for the science of sight, then for the painter's technique, and only later for a mental point of view.
intro.cn: perspective 是拉丁语 perspicere“看穿”名词化的结果。英语先用它指视觉的科学，再指画家的技法，最后才指心里的观点。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, see'. It is the root behind spectacle, inspect, respect, and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为“看、看见”。它是 spectacle、inspect、respect、perspective 的词根。

items.en: Perspicere was per- 'through' + specere 'look': 'to see through, look at closely, perceive clearly'.
items.cn: perspicere 是 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”：“看透、仔细看、清楚感知”。

items.en: Perspectiva was the medieval Latin term for the science of optics, literally 'the things of seeing through'.
items.cn: perspectiva 是中古拉丁语对光学的称呼，字面是“看穿的诸事”。

items.en: English takes perspective in the 14th century as the name of the optical science. It is a learned term before it is an everyday one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 perspective，作为光学学科的名称。它先是学术用语，后才进入日常。

items.en: The artistic sense, the technique of showing depth on a flat surface, is recorded by the 1590s. The scientific name becomes a painter's tool.
items.cn: 艺术义（在平面上表现纵深的技法）于 16 世纪 90 年代见于记录。学科名称变成了画家的工具。

items.en: The sense 'a view from a place' is recorded by the 1660s; the figurative 'mental point of view' by 1762. The metaphor of standing somewhere and looking is fully in place.
items.cn: “从某处看到的景色”义于 17 世纪 60 年代见于记录；比喻性的“心理观点”义于 1762 年。站在某处张望的比喻至此完全成形。

note.en: The first group shares the specere 'look' root; the second collects words for a way of seeing or judging.
note.cn: 第一组共享 specere“看”词根；第二组收“看事物的方式”类词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand things. It comes from the same perspicere but describes a person, not a viewpoint.
entries.definitionCN: 观察敏锐、理解快的。它同出 perspicere，但描述人，而不是视角。

entries.definition: having a ready insight into things; mentally sharp. A formal adjective from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物有敏锐洞察力的；心智锐利的。同出那个拉丁动词的正式形容词。

entries.definition: a possibility of a future event, or a view ahead. Pro- 'forward' + specere 'look'; the direction is forward, not through.
entries.definitionCN: 未来事件的可能性，或前方的景色。pro-“向前”+ specere“看”；方向是向前，不是穿透。

entries.definition: relating to perspective or to a point of view
entries.definitionCN: 与透视或视角有关的（由 perspective 派生）

entries.definition: a person's opinion or way of thinking. It is the everyday equivalent of perspective and lacks the art and depth senses.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的意见或思考方式。它是 perspective 的日常对应词，没有艺术与纵深的义项。

entries.definition: a position from which a subject is considered, often in debate. It keeps the physical 'standing place' image openly.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑某主题时所处的立场，常用于论辩。它明着保留“站立之处”的意象。

entries.definition: a way of approaching a subject, especially one chosen to make it interesting. It is more informal and tactical.
entries.definitionCN: 切入某主题的方式，尤指为使它有趣而选择的。它更口语、更具策略性。

entries.definition: a person's attitude to life, or a forecast. It is broader and often about mood rather than analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对生活的态度，或前景预测。它更宽，常关于情绪而非分析。

entries.definition: a position giving a good view. It is the literal place from which a perspective is obtained.
entries.definitionCN: 能获得良好视野的位置。它就是取得某种 perspective 的字面地点。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'through' + specere 'look', giving perspicere 'see through'. Family words perspective, perspectival, perspectivism; relatives prospect, inspect, respect, spectacle.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”，合成 perspicere“看透”。词族为 perspective、perspectival、perspectivism；亲属词 prospect、inspect、respect、spectacle。

normal.en: Spectare is 'look': perspective is looking through a particular opening.
normal.cn: spectare 是“看”：perspective 就是透过某个特定开口去看。

normal.en: Prospect looks forward, perspective looks through; same verb, different prefix.
normal.cn: prospect 向前看，perspective 穿透看；同一动词，不同前缀。

normal.en: Linear perspective was a Renaissance rule: parallels meet at a vanishing point.
normal.cn: 线性透视是文艺复兴的规则：平行线在消失点相交。

normal.en: In perspective means at the size the distance deserves.
normal.cn: in perspective 就是按距离应得的大小来看。

normal.en: Perspective-taking is imagination used as a measuring instrument.
normal.cn: 换位思考，是把想象力当量尺来用。

abstract.en: Perspective is not a better view; it is a different place to stand.
abstract.cn: 视角不是更好的视野，而是另一个站立之处。

abstract.en: Depth exists only because some things are allowed to be small.
abstract.cn: 纵深之所以存在，只因有些东西被允许变小。

abstract.en: The ability to change perspective is the cheapest form of mercy.
abstract.cn: 能换一个视角，是最廉价的慈悲。

examples.en: Try to see the decision from the perspective of a new employee.
examples.cn: 试着从新员工的角度看这个决定。

examples.en: The bad quarter should be put into perspective against ten years of growth.
examples.cn: 这个糟糕的季度应当放到十年增长的比例中来看。

examples.en: Brunelleschi's experiment demonstrated linear perspective in painting.
examples.cn: 布鲁内莱斯基的实验展示了绘画中的线性透视。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破视野·派克提夫”——派克提着窗框站定，换个位置就换一片视野 → perspective 视角、透视

root: 源自拉丁语 perspicere“看穿、看清”，由 per-“穿过”+ specere“看”构成；中世纪拉丁语 perspectiva 是“光学”，英语 14 世纪借入，16 世纪 90 年代转指绘画透视，1660 年代有“景色”义，1762 年才有比喻性的“观点”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of perspective, all one geometry: a viewpoint, a plane, and the lines that connect them.
sensesIntro.cn: perspective 的八个义项是同一个几何关系：一个视点、一个平面，以及连接二者的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye at a fixed point looking through a frame at a scene that recedes to a vanishing point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只眼固定在一点，透过窗框看出去，景物向消失点退去。

branches.en: MIND: where you stand and what you conclude — the viewpoint and the opinion it produces.
branches.cn: 心智：站在哪里与得出什么——视角以及由它产生的看法。

branches.en: EMPATHY: moving your own eye to another point, the viewpoint taken as an act.
branches.cn: 共情：把自己的眼移到另一点，视角由“位置”变成“动作”。

branches.en: PROPORTION: judging importance is drawing depth, and in perspective restores true size.
branches.cn: 比例：判断重要性就是画纵深，而 in perspective 是恢复真实大小。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE: the painter's vanishing point and the geometer's projection are one system, formalized.
branches.cn: 技法：画家的消失点与几何学家的投影，是同一个体系的形式化。

branches.en: LANDSCAPE: the oldest physical sense, what lies spread out in front of the eye.
branches.cn: 景物：最古老的物理义，铺展在眼前的那一片。

intro.en: Perspective's family is built on Latin specere 'to look'. Suffixes mark the adjective and the doctrine; compounds name the techniques and the mental acts.
intro.cn: perspective 的词族建立在拉丁语 specere“看”上。后缀标记形容词与学说；复合词则命名技法与心理活动。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are specere 'look', perspicere 'see through', and perspectiva, the medieval Latin name for optics.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 specere“看”、perspicere“看透”与 perspectiva——中世纪拉丁语对光学的称呼。

items.meaning: a viewpoint, or the art of showing depth
items.meaningCN: 视角；表现纵深的技法（来自拉丁语 perspectiva）
items.example: The two reports offer opposite perspectives.
items.exampleCN: 两份报告提供了相反的视角。

items.meaning: relating to a perspective or viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 与透视或视角有关的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The drawing has a strong perspectival structure.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画有很强的透视结构。

items.meaning: the view that knowledge is always from some perspective
items.meaningCN: 认为知识总是出自某种视角的主张（-ism 构成主义名词）
items.example: Nietzsche's perspectivism denies a view from nowhere.
items.exampleCN: 尼采的视角主义否认存在“无处之见”。

items.meaning: the act of imagining another person's viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 想象他人视角的行为（心理学用语）
items.exampleCN: 换位思考能减少团队冲突。

items.meaning: depth shown by lines converging on a vanishing point
items.meaningCN: 用线条汇聚于消失点来表现纵深（艺术术语）
items.example: The street is drawn in strict linear perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这条街用严格的线性透视画出。

items.meaning: depth shown by making distant things hazier and bluer
items.meaningCN: 通过使远处景物更朦胧、更偏蓝来表现纵深
items.example: The mountains fade by aerial perspective.
items.exampleCN: 群山因空气透视而渐淡。

items.meaning: seen at its true relative size or importance
items.meaningCN: 按真实的相对大小或重要性来看
items.example: The problem looks manageable in perspective.
items.exampleCN: 放到整体里看，问题并不难办。

items.meaning: to compare something so that its real importance becomes clear
items.meaningCN: 通过比较使某事的真实重要性显现
items.example: The figures put the loss into perspective.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字让损失的大小变得清楚。

items.meaning: a projection from a viewpoint that makes far things smaller
items.meaningCN: 从视点投射、使远处物体变小的投影法
items.example: Games use perspective projection to create depth.
items.exampleCN: 游戏用透视投影制造纵深。

items.meaning: a drawing made according to the rules of depth
items.example: The class began with perspective drawing.

definition_zh: 阶段；时期；月相；相位；相；分阶段实施；逐步引入或淘汰
definition_en: a distinct stage in a process or cycle; the state a regularly changing system has reached at a given moment; to carry something out in planned stages
core_image: 月亮走完一圈，被切成一块块叫得出名字的明暗形状
scene: The project moved into its final phase, when real users test the software.
sceneCN: 这里 phase 是「长过程中的一段」（第 1 个义项：阶段）；句意：项目进入最后阶段，由真实用户测试软件。场景要点：时间轴被切成几段、最后一段、用户试用。

pos.zh: 分阶段实施；使（系统）同步

derivatives.zh: 分阶段的；按计划逐步进行的

senses.title: A stage in a process
senses.titleCN: 阶段：长过程中的一段
senses.definition: one distinct part of a process that has several successive parts
senses.definitionCN: 一个有先后多个环节的过程中，界限清楚的其中一段
senses.example: The first phase of the trial focuses on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 试验的第一阶段重点关注安全性。
senses.why: The word starts from the moon: its endless cycle is cut into named segments. Any long human process is cut the same way, so one segment is a phase.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起于月亮：月亮无休止的循环被切成一段段有名字的形状。人类的任何长期过程也被同样地切开，于是一段就是一个 phase。

senses.title: A period with a shared character
senses.titleCN: 时期：一段有共同特征的岁月
senses.definition: a period in a person's life or in history that has a particular character
senses.definitionCN: 个人生活或历史中具有某种共同特征的一段时间
senses.example: As a teenager he went through a rebellious phase.
senses.exampleCN: 十几岁时他经历过一段叛逆期。
senses.why: Here the slice is marked off not by an external schedule but by shared mood or behaviour. The boundary is drawn by likeness, not by a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这里的切片不是由外部日程划出的，而是由共同的情绪或行为划出的。界线由相似性决定，而非计划。

senses.title: The moon's apparent shape
senses.titleCN: 月相：月亮露出的那张脸
senses.definition: the shape of the moon or another planet as it appears to us at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 月亮或其他行星在某一时刻呈现给我们的形状
senses.example: A thin crescent is the phase just after the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 细细的蛾眉月是新月之后的那个月相。
senses.why: This is the literal source. Greek phasis means appearance, and the moon is the thing whose appearance changes most visibly night after night.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义来源。希腊语 phasis 意为“显现”，而月亮正是夜复一夜外观变化最明显的那个东西。

senses.title: Physics: position in a wave cycle
senses.titleCN: 相位：波走到一圈的哪个位置
senses.definition: the point that a wave or oscillation has reached in its repeating cycle, measured as an angle
senses.definitionCN: 波或振动在重复循环中到达的位置，用角度来量度
senses.example: The two signals are in phase, so their peaks arrive together.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个信号同相，所以它们的波峰同时到达。
senses.why: A cycle can be drawn as a circle. Where you stand on that circle is your phase, so the moon idea becomes a measurable coordinate.
senses.whyCN: 一个循环可以画成一个圆。你站在那个圆上的位置就是相位，于是月亮的意象变成了可测量的坐标。

senses.title: Chemistry: a distinct state of matter
senses.titleCN: 相：同一条件下的一个物质状态
senses.definition: a state of matter, such as solid, liquid, or gas, that is distinct from other states present in the same system
senses.definitionCN: 同一体系中与其他状态明显不同的物质状态，如固、液、气
senses.example: Ice floating on water is a two-phase system.
senses.exampleCN: 浮在水上的冰构成一个两相体系。
senses.why: Inside one state the material is uniform, like one face of the moon. Crossing a visible boundary puts you in another phase.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个状态内部，物质是均匀的，就像月亮的同一张脸。越过一条可见的界线，就进入了另一个相。

senses.title: To carry out in planned stages
senses.titleCN: 分阶段实施：把整件事拆成几段来办
senses.definition: to organize an activity or change so that it happens in a series of planned stages
senses.definitionCN: 把一项活动或变革组织成一系列按计划推进的阶段
senses.example: The company will phase the new software into its offices over six months.
senses.exampleCN: 公司将在六个月内把新软件分阶段引入各个办公室。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: you treat a process as named slices and then perform the slices one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 名词动用：把过程当成一片片有名字的切片，再一片一片地执行。

senses.title: To introduce or remove gradually
senses.titleCN: 逐步引入／淘汰：一段一段地来
senses.definition: to bring something in or take it out gradually, stage by stage, instead of all at once
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次性，而是逐阶段地引入或撤出某物
senses.example: The old buses were phased out and replaced by electric ones.
senses.exampleCN: 旧公交车被逐步淘汰，换成了电动车。
senses.why: Phase in and phase out differ only in direction. Both keep every step small so that no single change is disruptive.
senses.whyCN: phase in 与 phase out 只差方向。两者都把每一步做小，使任何单次变化都不至于造成震荡。

senses.title: One aspect of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 侧面：事物露给人的那一面
senses.definition: one part or aspect of a situation, especially the part that shows at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 一个情况的某一部分或某一方面，尤指某一时刻显露出来的那一面
senses.example: They studied only one phase of the problem, ignoring its economic side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们只研究了问题的一个侧面，忽略了其经济面。
senses.why: Phasis is appearance. Whatever shows itself at a given moment is one face of a larger object that has other faces.
senses.whyCN: phasis 是“显现”。在某一刻显现出来的，总是一个更大事物的其中一张脸，它还有别的脸。

intro.en: Phase began as an astronomer's word for the moon's changing face. From there it spread to any cycle cut into stages, and finally to any aspect of anything.
intro.cn: phase 起初是天文学家用来称月亮变换的脸的术语。由此扩及任何被切成阶段的循环，最后泛指任何事物的一个侧面。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to show, bring to light'. It comes from PIE *bha- 'to shine', the same family that gives English beacon and the Greek root behind phenomenon and emphasis.
items.cn: phainein 意为“显现、带到光下”。它来自原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，同族词包括英语 beacon，以及 phenomenon、emphasis 背后的希腊词根。

items.en: From phainein came phasis, 'appearance', used especially of a star or the moon showing itself. The noun describes the act of appearing and the shape that appears.
items.cn: 由 phainein 生出 phasis“显现”，多用于星辰或月亮出现在天空中。这个名词既指显现的动作，也指显现出来的形状。

items.en: Greek astronomers spoke of the phases of the moon because its visible shape changes in a regular cycle. The term was technical before it was general.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家说月亮的 phases，因为它的可见形状按固定周期变化。这个词先是专业术语，后来才泛化。

items.en: Latin took phasis as a learned borrowing from Greek, keeping its astronomical sense. English received it through this Latin channel rather than directly.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 phasis 作为学术借词从希腊语引入，保留了天文学含义。英语是经这条拉丁渠道而非直接从希腊语接手的。

items.en: Phase of the moon is recorded in the 1660s. The general sense 'stage of development' appears in the 19th century, and the physics sense of wave phase follows in the same period.
items.cn: phase of the moon 的用法记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。“发展阶段”的泛义出现在 19 世纪，物理学上的“波相位”也同期出现。

items.en: Chemistry adopted phase for a distinct state of matter, and engineering adopted phase in and phase out for staged change. All of them keep the original picture: a cycle sliced into named parts.
items.cn: 化学用 phase 指一种独立的物质状态，工程领域用 phase in／phase out 指分阶段变更。这些用法都保留了原初画面：一个循环被切成有名字的几份。

note.en: The first group is built on near-identical spelling, only one of which shares the Greek root. The second group collects words for stages and aspects, each from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组拼写相近，其中只有一个与希腊词根同源。第二组收表示“阶段、方面”的词，但各自角度不同。

entries.definition: a group of words that forms a unit. It comes from Greek phrasis 'expression', from phrazein 'to point out, explain', not from phainein.
entries.definitionCN: 由一组词构成的单位。它来自希腊语 phrasis“表达”，动词 phrazein“指出、说明”，并非来自 phainein。

entries.definition: a rotating vector used to represent a wave, named directly from phase plus the -or agent ending.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表示波的旋转矢量，直接由 phase 加表施动者的 -or 构成。

entries.definition: arranged or carried out in stages. It is the past participle of the verb phase used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 按阶段安排或实施的。它是动词 phase 的过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: the gradual removal of something, formed from the verb phrase phase out.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步撤除某物，由动词短语 phase out 构成的复合名词。

entries.definition: a point or period in a process. Stage stresses the level reached, while phase stresses the bounded slice and often implies a cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 过程中的一个点或一段。stage 强调达到的程度，phase 强调有界的切片，且常含周期性。

entries.definition: a length of time with a defined beginning and end. Period is purely about time; phase also carries the idea of a distinct state or stage.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确起点和终点的一段时间。period 只谈时间；phase 还带有“独立状态或阶段”的意思。

entries.definition: one action in a sequence. A step is what you do; a phase is the stretch of time in which you do it.
entries.definitionCN: 序列中的一个动作。step 是你做的动作；phase 是做这件事的那段时间。

entries.definition: one part or feature of a situation. Aspect fits sense 08 closely; both come from roots meaning 'to look'.
entries.definitionCN: 情况的一个部分或特征。aspect 与第 8 义项最贴近，两者词根都含“看”的意思。

entries.definition: the condition something is in at a given time. State is static; phase is a position within a changing cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 某物在某一时刻所处的状况。state 是静态的；phase 是变化循环中的位置。

normalIntro.en: Five concrete hooks: the moon, the sliced timeline, the in/out pair, the synchronized waves, and the face behind the Greek word.
normalIntro.cn: 五个具体抓手：月亮、被切分的时间轴、进与出的一对、同步的波、以及希腊词背后那张脸。

normal.en: PHASE = the moon's face. Picture eight named moons hanging on a string.
normal.cn: PHASE＝月亮的脸。想象八个有名字的月亮挂在一条绳上。

normal.en: Take a long timeline and cut it into thick slices. Each slice has a name; each name is a phase.
normal.cn: 把一条长长的时间轴切成厚片。每一片都有名字，每个名字就是一个 phase。

normal.en: Phase in: slices come in from the left. Phase out: slices leave to the right.
normal.cn: phase in：切片从左边进来；phase out：切片从右边退出。

normal.en: In phase means two waves raise their hands at the same moment. Out of phase means one is early.
normal.cn: in phase 是两个波在同一刻举手；out of phase 是一个来早了。

normal.en: Phase and face are cousins in meaning: both are about what shows. The moon changes face; we name its faces as phases.
normal.cn: phase 与 face 在意思上是亲戚：都关乎“显现出来的样子”。月亮换脸，我们把这些脸命名为 phase。

abstract.en: Any long thing can be treated as a circle cut into arcs; naming an arc is already a theory of the whole.
abstract.cn: 任何漫长之物都可以被看成切成弧段的圆；给一段弧命名，本身就已经是对整体的理论。

abstract.en: A phase is a frozen frame from a film that never stops running.
abstract.cn: 一个 phase 是从一部永不停机的电影里截下来的一帧。

abstract.en: Boundaries between phases are drawn by observers, not found in nature; the cycle only becomes usable when we cut it.
abstract.cn: 阶段之间的界线是观察者画的，不是自然里现成的；只有切开，循环才变得可用。

examples.en: The negotiation entered a delicate phase after both sides had stated their positions.
examples.cn: 双方陈述立场之后，谈判进入了一个微妙的阶段。

examples.en: Engineers check that the two generators remain in phase before connecting them to the grid.
examples.cn: 工程师在把两台发电机接入电网前，要确认它们保持同相。

examples.en: The city plans to phase out diesel buses by 2030, replacing them route by route.
examples.cn: 这座城市计划到 2030 年逐步淘汰柴油公交，按线路逐条替换。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费兹”听起来像 face（脸）——月亮一夜换一张脸，换出的每张脸就是一个 phase（月相、阶段）

root: 希腊语 phainein“显现、照亮”→ phasis“显现（月相）”→ 拉丁 phasis → 英语 phase；与 phenomenon、emphasis、fantasy 同一条 phan- 线。

sensesIntro.en: Start from the moon and move outward: one visible shape, then one stretch of a cycle, then one stretch of any process, then one aspect of anything. The verb adds the idea of doing the slices one at a time.
sensesIntro.cn: 从月亮出发向外推：先是一个可见形状，再是一个循环中的一段，再是任何过程的一段，最后是任何事物的一个侧面。动词义则加上“一片一片地做”的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full moon cycle divided into named arcs, each arc showing a different face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整轮月相循环被切成有名字的弧段，每段露出不同的脸。

chain: A CYCLE CUT INTO NAMED SLICES
ONE SLICE FROZEN AT A MOMENT

branches.en: TIME: a slice of a process and a stretch of life share one boundary-drawing gesture.
branches.cn: 时间：过程的一段与人生的一段，共用同一个划界动作。

branches.en: MOON: the literal origin, the visible face that gave the word its name.
branches.cn: 月亮：本义来源，那个让这个词得名的可见的脸。

branches.en: SCIENCE: wave position and state of matter both turn the slice into a measurable coordinate.
branches.cn: 科学：波的位置与物质状态，都把切片变成可测量的坐标。

branches.en: ACTION: doing the slices in order, inward or outward.
branches.cn: 行动：按顺序做这些切片，向内引入或向外撤出。

branches.en: ASPECT: whatever shows at one moment is one face of a larger thing.
branches.cn: 侧面：某一刻显现出来的，总是更大事物的其中一张脸。

intro.en: The phase family is built on one Greek verb of showing, with prefixes that locate the showing (above, through) and suffixes that turn it into nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: phase 词族建立在一个表示“显现”的希腊动词上，前缀标明显现的位置（在上、穿过），后缀把它变成名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed these Greek forms whole, so the same pieces appear in Latin scientific vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这些希腊形式整体借入，所以同样的构件也出现在拉丁科技术语里。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或状态的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 顿悟（某种东西在顶上显现）
透明的（光能穿过去显现）
阶段的（较少用，多为 phasic 替代）

definition_zh: 现象；迹象；非凡的人或事；奇才
definition_en: a fact or event that can be observed, especially one that is unusual or not yet explained; also an extraordinary person or thing
core_image: 黑暗中忽然亮起一点，被眼睛稳稳接住
scene: Scientists still cannot explain the phenomenon of ball lightning.
sceneCN: 这里 phenomenon 是「可观察但尚未解释的事实」（第 1 个义项：现象）；句意：科学家至今无法解释球状闪电这一现象。场景要点：异常、被观测到、原因未知。

pos.zh: 现象；迹象；非凡的人或事

forms.label: 复数（指非凡人物时偶用）

derivatives.zh: 现象主义（认为人只能认识现象）

senses.title: An observable fact or event
senses.titleCN: 现象：能被观察到的某事
senses.definition: a fact or event that can be observed, especially one whose cause is not yet understood
senses.definitionCN: 可以被观察到的事实或事件，尤指原因尚未被理解的那种
senses.example: The northern lights are a phenomenon seen near the poles.
senses.exampleCN: 北极光是在极地附近能看到的一种现象。
senses.why: Greek phainomenon means that which appears. Anything that shows itself to the senses qualifies, whether or not we can explain it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phainomenon 意为“显现出来的东西”。凡向感官显现的都可算，无论我们能否解释它。

senses.title: Something unusual or unexplained
senses.titleCN: 异象：解释不了的那件事
senses.definition: an event that is strange, rare, or not yet explained by science
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪的、罕见的、或科学尚未解释的事件
senses.example: Reports of the phenomenon spread faster than any explanation could.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这一异象的报道传播得比任何解释都快。
senses.why: The word's everyday weight shifted toward the unusual: if it appears and we cannot account for it, we call it a phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的日常重心转向“不寻常”：如果它显现了而我们说不清，就称它为 phenomenon。

senses.title: An event of the natural world
senses.titleCN: 自然现象：大地自己演出的那一幕
senses.definition: a regularly occurring event of the physical world, such as weather, tides, or growth
senses.definitionCN: 物理世界中规律发生的事件，如天气、潮汐或生长
senses.example: Migration is a phenomenon driven by season and food supply.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙是由季节和食物供给驱动的自然现象。
senses.why: Nature is the first place where things show themselves without human arrangement, so natural events became the model case.
senses.whyCN: 自然界是最早出现“无需人为安排就自行显现”的地方，因此自然事件成了典范情形。

senses.title: Philosophy: an object of experience
senses.titleCN: 哲学：呈现给意识的对象
senses.definition: in philosophy, anything that appears to consciousness, as opposed to the thing as it is in itself
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指呈现于意识中的一切，以区别于物自身
senses.example: Kant argued that we know phenomena, not things in themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 康德主张我们认识的是现象，而非物自体。
senses.why: Philosophy kept the literal Greek sense: the phenomenon is exactly what appears, and the question is what lies behind the appearance.
senses.whyCN: 哲学保留了希腊本义：现象正是显现出来的那个东西，问题在于显现背后还有什么。

senses.title: Medicine: a sign or symptom
senses.titleCN: 医学：看得见的征候
senses.definition: a sign or symptom that can be observed in a patient and points to a condition
senses.definitionCN: 在病人身上可以观察到、并指向某种病情的体征或症状
senses.example: Raynaud's phenomenon makes the fingers turn white in the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 雷诺现象使手指在寒冷中变白。
senses.why: A symptom is something that shows itself on the body. Medicine names the visible sign rather than the hidden cause.
senses.whyCN: 症状就是显现在身体上的东西。医学命名的是可见的征象，而不是隐藏的病因。

senses.title: An extraordinary person or thing
senses.titleCN: 奇人奇物：本身就是一件异象
senses.definition: a person or thing that is so remarkable that it seems to belong to a different order
senses.definitionCN: 非凡到仿佛属于另一类事物的人或物
senses.example: By fifteen she was a phenomenon in the chess world.
senses.exampleCN: 十五岁时她已是国际象棋界的奇才。
senses.why: If a person appears among ordinary people the way a marvel appears among ordinary events, the same word fits.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人出现在常人之中，就像奇观出现在寻常事件之中，同一个词就适用。

senses.title: A class of observable facts
senses.titleCN: 现象总称：成类的一批显现
senses.definition: the whole range of observable facts in a field, usually in the plural phenomena
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域内可观察事实的总和，通常用复数 phenomena
senses.example: The book surveys electrical phenomena in the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书综述了大气中的电现象。
senses.why: Greek plural phenomena was borrowed along with the singular. English uses the plural for a set of related appearances studied together.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语复数 phenomena 与单数一同被借入。英语用复数指一组放在一起研究的相关显现。

senses.title: A wonder to be witnessed
senses.titleCN: 奇观：值得亲眼一看的显现
senses.definition: something impressive that draws attention and seems worth seeing for itself
senses.definitionCN: 引人注目、本身值得一看的了不起之物
senses.example: The total eclipse was a phenomenon no one in the crowd would forget.
senses.exampleCN: 那次日全食是人群中无人会忘记的奇观。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply 'that which shows'. When what shows is overwhelming, the word slides toward spectacle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层只是“显现出来的东西”。当显现之物压倒地引人注目时，词义便滑向“奇观”。

intro.en: Phenomenon is a Greek philosophical term carried into English through Latin. Its base verb means to bring something into the light, and its spelling still carries the Greek plural.
intro.cn: phenomenon 是一个经拉丁语传入英语的希腊哲学术语。其底层动词意为“把某物带到光下”，其拼写至今保留希腊语复数。

items.en: Phainein meant 'to bring to light, show'. It descends from PIE *bha- 'to shine', the same source as English beacon and the root behind emphasis and fantasy.
items.cn: phainein 意为“带到光下、显现”。它源自原始印欧语 *bha-“发光”，与英语 beacon 以及 emphasis、fantasy 的词根同源。

items.en: The passive participle of phainesthai 'to appear' was phainomenon, literally 'that which appears'. Philosophers used it for whatever is given to the senses.
items.cn: phainesthai“显现”的被动分词是 phainomenon，字面即“显现出来的东西”。哲学家用它指一切呈现给感官之物。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek word as phaenomenon, keeping the philosophical sense. The ae spelling survives in the English plural phenomena.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把希腊词借作 phaenomenon，保留哲学含义。其中的 ae 拼法在英语复数 phenomena 里仍有痕迹。

items.en: English records phenomenon in the 1570s as a learned term. The plural phenomena was borrowed with it, which is why it does not follow the regular English -s pattern.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 70 年代把 phenomenon 记录为学术用语，复数 phenomena 一并借入，所以它不按英语常规加 -s。

items.en: The sense 'extraordinary occurrence' is recorded in 1771, and the philosophical sense tied to Kant's usage spreads in the 1780s and after.
items.cn: “非凡事件”这一义项记录于 1771 年；与康德用法相关的哲学义在 18 世纪 80 年代及以后传播开来。

items.en: Modern English uses the singular for one event and phenomena for several. The informal plural phenomenons appears mainly for the 'remarkable person' sense and is often criticized.
items.cn: 现代英语用单数指一个事件，用 phenomena 指多个。非正式的 phenomenons 主要用于“非凡人物”义，且常受批评。

note.en: The first group shows the same Greek root in different dress. The second group collects words for things that happen or things that are seen.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个希腊词根的不同装束。第二组收表示“发生之事”或“被看见之物”的词。

entries.definition: the Greek plural of phenomenon. It is a plural noun, not a singular, so one should not say a phenomena.
entries.definitionCN: phenomenon 的希腊式复数。它是复数名词而非单数，因此不应说 a phenomena。

entries.definition: relating to phenomena, or extraordinary. The adjective adds -al to the stem phenomen-.
entries.definitionCN: 与现象有关的，或非凡的。形容词由词干 phenomen- 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: a ghost or an illusion. It comes from Greek phantasma, from phainein 'to show', the same root as phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 幽灵或幻象。它来自希腊语 phantasma，源于 phainein“显现”，与 phenomenon 同根。

entries.definition: an illusion or a product of imagination. It preserves more of the Greek phantasma than phantom does.
entries.definitionCN: 幻象或想象的产物。它比 phantom 保留了更多希腊语 phantasma 的原形。

entries.definition: something that happens. Event is neutral; phenomenon adds the idea of being observed and often of being puzzling.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的事情。event 中性；phenomenon 多出“被观察到”以及“常令人费解”的意思。

entries.definition: something that takes place. Occurrence simply records that it happened, without implying study or wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的事。occurrence 只记录它发生了，不含研究或惊奇的意味。

entries.definition: something that causes wonder. Marvel stresses the observer's amazement; phenomenon can be neutral and scientific.
entries.definitionCN: 引起惊奇的事物。marvel 强调观察者的惊叹；phenomenon 可以是中性的、科学的。

entries.definition: something that is seen, especially something unusual. Sight focuses on the visual impression, phenomenon on the fact observed.
entries.definitionCN: 所见之物，尤指不寻常的。sight 侧重视觉印象，phenomenon 侧重被观察的事实。

entries.definition: something known to be true. Fact is about truth claims; phenomenon is about appearance to an observer.
entries.definitionCN: 已知为真之事。fact 关乎真假判断；phenomenon 关乎对观察者的显现。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the light in the dark, the Greek plural, the Kantian split, the medical sign, and the child prodigy.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：黑暗中的光、希腊式复数、康德的分野、医学体征、少年奇才。

normal.en: Phenomenon = something that switches on in the dark and the eye catches it. Phan- in Greek means to show.
normal.cn: phenomenon＝在黑暗中亮起、被眼睛接住的东西。希腊语 phan- 就是“显现”。

normal.en: One phenomenon, two phenomena. Treat the -a as a Greek passport stamp, not as a mistake.
normal.cn: 一个 phenomenon，两个 phenomena。把词尾的 -a 看成希腊护照上的章，而不是拼写错误。

normal.en: Kant's slogan: we see phenomena, we never see the thing itself. The word is literally 'the appearing'.
normal.cn: 康德的口号：我们看见现象，看不见物自体。这个词字面就是“显现者”。

normal.en: A doctor reads phenomena on the body: white fingers in the cold are a phenomenon pointing to a hidden cause.
normal.cn: 医生读身体上的现象：寒冷中发白的手指就是一个指向隐藏病因的 phenomenon。

normal.en: Call a fifteen-year-old chess genius a phenomenon and you are saying she appears among us like a marvel among events.
normal.cn: 把十五岁的棋童称为 phenomenon，等于说她出现在我们中间，就像奇观出现在寻常事件中。

abstract.en: A phenomenon is the world's surface; the thing in itself is the world's depth. The word marks the limit of what can be shown.
abstract.cn: 现象是世界的表面，物自体是世界的深处。这个词标记的是“能被显现”的边界。

abstract.en: What counts as a phenomenon depends on who is looking and with what instrument; the observed is never wholly separate from the observer.
abstract.cn: 什么算作现象，取决于谁在看、用什么在看；被观察者从不与观察者完全分离。

abstract.en: Naming a phenomenon is the first act of science and already a theory: to pick it out is to decide what matters.
abstract.cn: 命名一个现象是科学的第一步，也已经是理论：挑出它，就是决定了什么才算重要。

examples.en: The migration of monarch butterflies is a phenomenon that still puzzles biologists.
examples.cn: 帝王蝶迁徙是至今仍让生物学家困惑的现象。

examples.en: In the 1960s the Beatles became a global phenomenon, not merely a band.
examples.cn: 20 世纪 60 年代，披头士成了全球性现象，而不仅仅是一支乐队。

examples.en: Phenomena observed at one temperature do not always hold at another.
examples.cn: 在某一温度下观察到的现象，未必在另一温度下成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费诺米农”——费诺在米农面前亮出一盏灯，众人看见一个现象（phenomenon）

root: 希腊语 phainein“显现、照亮”→ phainomenon“显现出来的东西”→ 晚期拉丁 phaenomenon → 英语 phenomenon；与 phase、emphasis、phantom、fantasy 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means what shows itself. From that base it spreads in two directions: toward the scientific fact to be explained, and toward the marvel that overwhelms the observer. The plural phenomena is Greek, not English.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“显现出来的东西”。由此向两个方向展开：一是待解释的科学事实，二是压倒地引人惊叹的奇观。复数 phenomena 是希腊式的，不是英语式的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a point of light in the dark, appearing to an eye that did not make it.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中的一点光，向一只并未制造它的眼睛显现。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: the neutral fact, natural or social, that anyone can notice.
branches.cn: 观察：中性的、任何人都能注意到的事实，自然的或社会的。

branches.en: PUZZLE: the same fact weighted with strangeness because no explanation is available.
branches.cn: 谜团：同一事实因缺乏解释而被加上了“怪异”的重量。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: appearance as such, set against the thing in itself.
branches.cn: 哲学：显现本身，与物自体相对而立。

branches.en: WITNESS: the sign read on a body and the spectacle watched by a crowd — appearance as evidence or as show.
branches.cn: 见证：身上读出的征候与众人围观的奇观——显现作为证据或作为演出。

branches.en: CLASS: a remarkable being, and the plural set of appearances studied together.
branches.cn: 类别：非凡的存在者，以及被放在一起研究的一批显现。

intro.en: Phenomenon is the most literal member of the phan- family: a passive participle turned noun, then fitted with English adjective and discipline suffixes.
intro.cn: phenomenon 是 phan- 词族里最字面的成员：一个被动分词变成名词，再装上英语的形容词与学科后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin kept the Greek participle intact, which is why the English word looks Greek rather than English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊分词原样保留，所以英语词看起来像希腊语而不像英语。

items.meaningCN: 表示“被……的”的被动分词后缀
希腊语中性单数名词词尾
以 -on 结尾名词的希腊式复数词尾
表示学说或体系的词尾

definition_zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；哲理；达观
definition_en: the study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, values, and reason; a system of ideas held by a person or group
core_image: 一个人放下手里的急事，转身追问「这一切究竟凭什么」
scene: Her philosophy is simple: work hard and stay curious.
sceneCN: 这里 philosophy 是「一个人奉行的人生准则」（第 3 个义项：准则）；句意：她的人生准则很简单：努力工作，保持好奇。场景要点：不是学科、是一套自持的态度。

pos.zh: 哲学；思想体系；人生准则；达观

senses.title: The academic study of first questions
senses.titleCN: 哲学学科：追问最根本的问题
senses.definition: the academic study of the most basic questions about existence, knowledge, truth, values, and reason
senses.definitionCN: 对存在、知识、真理、价值与理性等最根本问题的学术研究
senses.example: She took up philosophy after a first course in logic.
senses.exampleCN: 上完一门逻辑学入门课之后，她开始研读哲学。
senses.why: The Greek word names a love of wisdom. A discipline that pursues wisdom for its own sake became a faculty, then a degree subject.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词本意是“爱智慧”。一门为智慧本身而追求智慧的学问，后来成了一个学科门类、一个学位专业。

senses.title: A system of thought
senses.titleCN: 思想体系：一套自成一体的说法
senses.definition: a particular system of ideas about the world, often named after its founder
senses.definitionCN: 关于世界的一套特定观念体系，常以其创立者命名
senses.example: His early work was shaped by German idealist philosophy.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的工作受到德国唯心主义哲学体系的影响。
senses.why: A discipline that keeps asking first questions produces rival answers. Each coherent set of answers becomes a philosophy with a name.
senses.whyCN: 一门不停追问根本问题的学科会产出彼此竞争的答案。每一套自洽的答案就变成了一个有名字的哲学体系。

senses.title: Guiding principles for living
senses.titleCN: 人生准则：拿来过日子的一套道理
senses.definition: the set of principles that guides a person's or an organization's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指导个人或组织行为的一套原则
senses.example: Our philosophy is to fix the cause, not just the symptom.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的准则是解决病根，而不只是处理症状。
senses.why: The grand system shrinks to the scale of one life. What a person treats as first principles becomes their working philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的体系缩到一个人的尺度。一个人当作根本原则的东西，就成了他行事的准则。

senses.title: Calm acceptance of difficulty
senses.titleCN: 达观：把坏事放回它该有的尺寸
senses.definition: a calm attitude toward trouble, based on seeing it as part of a larger picture
senses.definitionCN: 面对困顿时的一种平静态度，源于把它看成更大图景的一部分
senses.example: He accepted the loss with philosophy and went back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他达观地接受了损失，又回去工作了。
senses.why: The discipline trains you to see events against a wider frame. That habit, applied to daily misfortune, shows up as composure.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问训练你把事件放进更宽的框架里看。这个习惯用到日常的不幸上，表现出来就是沉着。

senses.title: The philosophy of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某领域的哲学：先问这门学问凭什么
senses.definition: the critical study of the assumptions and methods of a particular subject, such as science, law, or history
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科（如科学、法律、历史）的前提与方法所作的批判性研究
senses.example: Philosophy of law asks what makes a rule legally valid.
senses.exampleCN: 法哲学追问：是什么使一条规则具有法律效力。
senses.why: Every field rests on assumptions it cannot prove from inside. Philosophy is called in to examine those foundations.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都建立在它内部无法证明的前提上。哲学被请来检查这些地基。

senses.title: The principles behind a practice
senses.titleCN: 理念：一套做法背后的道理
senses.definition: the set of ideas and aims that explain why something is done the way it is
senses.definitionCN: 解释某件事为何这样做的一套观念与目标
senses.example: The school's philosophy of teaching puts questions before answers.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校的教学理念把问题放在答案之前。
senses.why: Any practice can be asked for its rationale. The rationale, stated as principles, is its philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 任何做法都可以被追问理由。把这些理由表述为原则，就是它的理念。

senses.title: The ancient love of wisdom
senses.titleCN: 爱智：最早的那种生活方式
senses.definition: the original Greek pursuit of wisdom through reasoned inquiry, before it became an academic subject
senses.definitionCN: 希腊人最早通过理性探究追求智慧的生活方式，尚在它成为学科之前
senses.example: In Plato's dialogues, philosophy is a way of life rather than a job.
senses.exampleCN: 在柏拉图的对话里，哲学是一种生活方式而不是一份职业。
senses.why: Philosophia literally means love of wisdom. The historical sense keeps the desire rather than the syllabus.
senses.whyCN: philosophia 字面就是“爱智慧”。这个历史义保留的是那份渴望，而不是课程表。

senses.title: The habit of questioning assumptions
senses.titleCN: 追问前提：不接受「向来如此」
senses.definition: a critical habit of asking what an accepted belief rests on
senses.definitionCN: 一种批判性的习惯：追问一个被接受的看法究竟依托于什么
senses.example: Bring some philosophy to the meeting and ask why this rule exists.
senses.exampleCN: 带点哲学思辨进会场，问问这条规定为什么存在。
senses.why: Strip away the subject matter and what remains is a move: refuse to let a premise pass unexamined.
senses.whyCN: 剥掉具体内容，剩下的就是一个动作：不让任何一个前提未经检查就过关。

intro.en: Philosophy is a Greek compound meaning love of wisdom. The word names an attitude before it names a subject, and English borrowed it through Latin and French.
intro.cn: philosophy 是一个意为“爱智慧”的希腊复合词。它先命名的是一种态度，后来才命名一门学科；英语是经拉丁语和法语接手的。

items.en: Philos meant 'dear, beloved, loving'. It described affection and close friendship rather than abstract approval.
items.cn: philos 意为“亲爱的、被爱的、爱着的”。它描述的是亲近与友情，而不是抽象的赞同。

items.en: Sophia meant 'wisdom, skill, cleverness'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; some sources connect it with sophos 'wise' and possibly with words for clarity. This part of the chain is not firmly established.
items.cn: sophia 意为“智慧、技艺、聪明”。它更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与 sophos“智慧的”以及表示“清楚”的词联系起来。这一段词源链并无定论。

items.en: Philos plus sophia gave philosophia, 'the love of wisdom'. The word is associated with Pythagoras by later ancient reports, though the attribution is traditional rather than documented.
items.cn: philos 加 sophia 构成 philosophia“爱智慧”。后世古籍把这个词与毕达哥拉斯联系起来，但这属于传统说法，缺乏直接文献证据。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word unchanged in sense. Cicero and others used it for the Greek tradition of reasoned inquiry.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样借入这个希腊词，含义不变。西塞罗等人用它来指希腊那条理性探究的传统。

items.en: Old French shortened and reshaped the word as filosofie, which is the form English received around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语把词形缩短、改造为 filosofie，英语约在 1300 年接受的就是这个形式。

items.en: From the 19th century the word also names a university department and its curriculum. The older sense of a way of life survives in phrases like with philosophy.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，这个词也指大学的院系及其课程。较古老的“生活方式”义则保存在 with philosophy 这类短语里。

note.en: The first group shares the philo- or soph- pieces but not always the whole meaning. The second group collects words for systems of belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享 philo- 或 soph- 构件，但未必整体同义。第二组收表示信仰体系的词。

entries.definition: a person who studies or practises philosophy. Philosophy plus -er, the person who loves wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 研究或实践哲学的人。philosophy 加 -er，即爱智慧的人。

entries.definition: relating to philosophy, or calm in the face of trouble. The adjective covers both the academic and the composed senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与哲学有关的，或面对困顿时平静的。这个形容词同时覆盖学科义与达观义。

entries.definition: the study of language and texts historically. Philo- 'loving' plus logos 'word', so 'love of words', not love of wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 对语言与文本的历史研究。philo-“爱”加 logos“言词”，是“爱言词”，不是爱智慧。

entries.tag: 同 soph- 根 · 贬义
entries.definition: clever but misleading argument. From sophos 'wise', but the word marks cleverness used to deceive rather than wisdom.
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙却误导人的论证。源自 sophos“智慧的”，但这个词标记的是用于欺骗的机巧，而非智慧。

entries.definition: the activity or product of thinking. Thought is broader and looser; philosophy is organized and argues from principles.
entries.definitionCN: 思考活动或其产物。thought 更宽更松；philosophy 是有组织、从原则出发论证的。

entries.definition: a system of beliefs held by a group, often political. Ideology stresses shared social belief; philosophy stresses reasoned inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 群体持有的一套信念，常指政治的。ideology 强调群体共享的信念；philosophy 强调理性探究。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by a religion or school. Doctrine is received and taught; philosophy invites challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教或学派所传授的一套信念。doctrine 是被接受、被讲授的；philosophy 则欢迎质疑。

entries.definition: the overall way a person sees the world. Worldview can be unspoken and unexamined; philosophy is the examined version.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看世界的总体方式。worldview 可以是未言明、未检查的；philosophy 是经过检查的版本。

entries.definition: the basic rules a person follows. Principles are the content; philosophy is the reasoned framework that holds them together.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人遵循的基本规则。principles 是内容；philosophy 是把它们统摄起来的理性框架。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the two Greek halves, the Pythagoras story, the difference from philology, the calm acceptance, and the meeting-room question.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：两个希腊半边、毕达哥拉斯的传说、与 philology 的区别、达观、以及会议室里的那一问。

normal.en: Philo- = loving, -sophy = wisdom. Philosophy is love of wisdom, spelled out in two halves.
normal.cn: philo-＝爱，-sophy＝智慧。philosophy 就是“爱智慧”，两个半边拼得明明白白。

normal.en: Pythagoras is said to have coined it: he called himself a lover of wisdom, not a possessor of it.
normal.cn: 据说毕达哥拉斯造了这个词：他称自己是智慧的热爱者，而不是占有者。

normal.en: Philology loves words, philosophy loves wisdom. Same prefix, different object.
normal.cn: philology 爱言词，philosophy 爱智慧。前缀相同，对象不同。

normal.en: With philosophy means carrying trouble lightly, as if it were one small item in a very large frame.
normal.cn: with philosophy 是把困顿拿得很轻，仿佛它只是一个极大画框里的小物件。

normal.en: In a meeting, philosophy is the person who asks why this rule exists at all.
normal.cn: 在会上，philosophy 就是那个问“这条规定到底为什么存在”的人。

abstract.en: Philosophy is what remains when you refuse to let any premise pass without asking what holds it up.
abstract.cn: 哲学就是当你拒绝让任何前提未经追问就过关时，剩下的那种活动。

abstract.en: A philosophy is a map of the whole drawn by someone who has never seen the whole.
abstract.cn: 一套哲学是一个从未见过整体的人画出的整体地图。

abstract.en: Wisdom is not a possession one can hold; the word's geometry is a reaching toward, not an arrival.
abstract.cn: 智慧不是可以握有的东西；这个词的几何形状是“伸向”，而不是“抵达”。

examples.en: He studied philosophy for four years before turning to artificial intelligence.
examples.cn: 他学了四年哲学，之后转向人工智能。

examples.en: Their company philosophy is that a slow correct decision beats a fast wrong one.
examples.cn: 他们的公司理念是：慢慢做对的决定胜过匆匆做错的决定。

examples.en: She took the criticism with philosophy and revised the paper that same week.
examples.cn: 她达观地接受了批评，并在同一周修改了论文。

dict_mnemonic.text: “费罗索菲”——费罗（philo，爱）追着索菲（sophia，智慧）跑，一路追问到底，就是哲学

root: 希腊语 philosophia＝philos“爱”+ sophia“智慧”；经拉丁 philosophia、古法语 filosofie 进入英语（约 1300 年）。sophia 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as an attitude (love of wisdom), hardens into a discipline, splits into rival systems, and then shrinks back down to one person's working principles or one field's foundations. The calm sense is the attitude applied to daily trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起于一种态度（爱智慧），固化为学科，分化为彼此竞争的体系，再缩回一个人的行事原则或一个领域的地基。达观义则是把这种态度用到日常困顿上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person setting down urgent business to ask what everything rests on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人放下急务，转去追问一切究竟依托于什么。

chain: A PERSONAL CREED OR FIELD'S FOUNDATION

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the academic subject and the ancient way of life are the same pursuit, institutionalized or not.
branches.cn: 学科：学院里的科目与古代的生活方式是同一种追求，只是是否被制度化。

branches.en: SYSTEM: coherent answers harden into named schools.
branches.cn: 体系：自洽的答案凝固成有名字的学派。

branches.en: GUIDANCE: the grand system scaled down to a person's creed or an institution's rationale.
branches.cn: 指导：宏大体系缩到个人的准则或机构的理念。

branches.en: COMPOSURE: the wide frame applied to daily misfortune, which shows up as calm.
branches.cn: 达观：把宽框架用到日常不幸上，表现为平静。

branches.en: CRITIQUE: examining a field's assumptions, and the habit of refusing unexamined premises.
branches.cn: 批判：检查一个领域的前提，以及拒绝未经检查的前提这一习惯。

intro.en: The family is built from two Greek nouns joined by a combining vowel, then extended with ordinary English endings for people, adjectives, and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词族由两个希腊名词加连接元音拼成，再用普通英语词尾扩展出人、形容词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed the compound through intact, so the Greek pieces remain visible in Latin and in every European borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个复合词原样传下，所以希腊构件在拉丁语以及欧洲各语言的借词里仍然可见。

items.meaning: knowledge or wisdom of a kind
to act in a way, to make

items.meaningCN: 表示信奉某学说者的后缀

items.exampleCN: 憎恶智慧（极少用，与 philosophy 相对）

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、活动或学科的名词后缀

definition_zh: 身体的；物质的；物理学的；有形的；需体力的；自然的；（名词）体检
definition_en: relating to the body, to material things, or to physics; existing in a form that can be touched; (noun) a medical examination
core_image: 伸手能摸到、有重量、会疼的那一层世界
scene: Regular physical activity keeps the heart and lungs strong.
sceneCN: 这里 physical 是「身体的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：规律的身体活动能让心肺保持强健。场景要点：筋骨、出汗、心跳，不是心理层面。

pos.zh: 身体的；物质的；物理学的；有形的；需体力的

forms.label: 比较级（更偏身体／更物质）
最高级（最偏身体／最物质）

senses.title: Relating to the body
senses.titleCN: 身体的：跟筋骨血肉有关
senses.definition: relating to a person's or animal's body rather than the mind
senses.definitionCN: 与人或动物的身体有关，而非与心智有关
senses.example: Regular physical activity keeps the heart and lungs strong.
senses.exampleCN: 规律的身体活动能让心肺保持强健。
senses.why: Greek physis means nature, and the body is the most immediate piece of nature we own. Physical first marked what belongs to the natural, visible self.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 意为“自然”，而身体是我们拥有的最直接的一块自然。physical 最早标记的就是属于这具可见的自然之身的东西。

senses.title: Relating to matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 物质的：由材料构成的那一面
senses.definition: relating to material things and their properties rather than to ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 与物质事物及其属性有关，而非与观念或感受有关
senses.example: The report describes the physical properties of the new alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了这种新合金的物理性质。
senses.why: From the body the word extends to anything that occupies space and can be measured: matter as opposed to meaning.
senses.whyCN: 从身体出发，这个词扩及一切占据空间、可被测量之物：物质，与意义相对。

senses.title: Relating to the science of physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学的：关于力、热、光、电的那门学问
senses.definition: belonging to physics, the science of matter, energy, and their interactions
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理学的，即研究物质、能量及其相互作用的科学
senses.example: Physical chemistry bridges the two departments.
senses.exampleCN: 物理化学把这两个系科连接起来。
senses.why: Physics took its name from the same Greek root. Anything studied by that science is physical in this narrower, technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理学（physics）的名字来自同一个希腊词根。被这门科学研究的东西，就在这个更窄的专业意义上属于 physical。

senses.title: Real and tangible
senses.titleCN: 有形的：真实存在、摸得着
senses.definition: existing in a real, material form that can be touched, seen, or measured
senses.definitionCN: 以真实的、物质的形态存在，可以被触摸、看见或测量
senses.example: The plan finally took physical form as a printed book.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划最终以一本印刷书的实体形态出现。
senses.why: If matter is what can be measured, then 'physical' becomes a guarantee of reality: not imagined, not merely promised.
senses.whyCN: 如果物质就是可被测量的东西，那么 physical 就成了“真实”的保证：不是想象，不只是承诺。

senses.title: Involving bodily force or contact
senses.titleCN: 动身体的：靠力气、会碰撞
senses.definition: involving bodily effort, contact, or force, as in sport or in violence
senses.definitionCN: 涉及身体用力、接触或强制，如体育或暴力场合
senses.example: Ice hockey is a far more physical game than badminton.
senses.exampleCN: 冰球比羽毛球激烈得多，身体对抗也多得多。
senses.why: Bodies in contact is the most visible kind of physical interaction, so the word comes to describe rough, hands-on activity.
senses.whyCN: 身体相互接触是最显眼的物理性互动，所以这个词被用来形容粗重的、动手动脚的活动。

senses.title: Belonging to the natural world
senses.titleCN: 自然的：山川气候，非人造
senses.definition: belonging to nature, especially in contrast with what humans build or arrange
senses.definitionCN: 属于自然界的，尤与人为建造或安排的事物相对
senses.example: Physical geography studies rivers, mountains, and climate.
senses.exampleCN: 自然地理学研究河流、山脉与气候。
senses.why: Physis is nature itself. This sense keeps the oldest meaning most faithfully: whatever is not made by us.
senses.whyCN: physis 就是“自然”。这个义项最忠实地保留了最古老的含义：非由我们制造的一切。

senses.title: Noun: a medical check-up
senses.titleCN: 名词：体检（口语）
senses.definition: a medical examination of the body, usually called a physical or a physical exam
senses.definitionCN: 对身体进行的医学检查，通常说 a physical 或 a physical exam
senses.example: She has her annual physical every September.
senses.exampleCN: 她每年九月做一次年度体检。
senses.why: The noun is short for physical examination. The adjective turned into a name for the event in which the body is examined.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 physical examination 的省略。形容词变成了那场“检查身体”的事件之名。

senses.title: Legal: material evidence
senses.titleCN: 法律：实物证据
senses.definition: in law, referring to objects and traces that can be examined, as opposed to testimony
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指可被检验的实物与痕迹，与证言相对
senses.example: Physical evidence placed him at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 实物证据表明他曾在现场。
senses.why: Courts separate what can be held and tested from what is only said. Physical marks the first category.
senses.whyCN: 法庭把可以拿在手里检验的东西与只是被说出来的话分开。physical 标记的是前一类。

intro.en: Physical descends from the Greek word for nature. Its story is the story of physis: first what grows, then the whole natural order, then the body, then matter itself.
