intro.cn: physical 源自希腊语中表示“自然”的那个词。它的历史就是 physis 的历史：先指生长之物，再指整个自然秩序，再指身体，最后指物质本身。

items.en: Phyein meant 'to grow, to bring forth'. It comes from PIE *bheu- 'to grow, to be', the root behind English be and build.
items.cn: phyein 意为“生长、生出”。它来自原始印欧语 *bheu-“生长、存在”，英语 be 与 build 也出自这条根。

items.en: Physis meant 'nature' but literally 'growth'. To the Greeks, a thing's nature was what it grew into when nothing interfered.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然”，字面却是“生长”。在希腊人看来，一物的自然就是它在不受干扰时会长成的样子。

items.en: Physikos meant 'natural, of nature', and also 'about natural things'. It described both the subject matter and the person who studied it.
items.cn: physikos 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“研究自然之物的”。它既描述研究对象，也描述研究的人。

items.en: Latin physicus meant 'natural' and, in later use, 'a physician'. Medieval physica covered medicine and natural philosophy together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physicus 意为“自然的”，后期也指“医生”。中世纪的 physica 把医学与自然哲学合在一起。

items.en: English physical appears in the 16th century with the sense 'of nature'. The sense 'of the body' follows within the same century, and the sense tied to the science of physics develops later.
items.cn: 英语 physical 出现于 16 世纪，意为“自然的”。“身体的”这一义在同一个世纪内跟进；与物理学这门科学相关的义项则更晚发展出来。

items.en: The modern word splits into the body (physical training), matter (physical properties), science (physical chemistry), and reality (physical evidence), all resting on the same Greek idea of nature.
items.cn: 现代这个词分向身体（physical training）、物质（physical properties）、科学（physical chemistry）与实在（physical evidence），全都依托同一个希腊的“自然”观念。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root for nature. The second group collects words for what is bodily or materially real.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示“自然”的希腊词根。第二组收表示“身体的”或“物质上真实”的词。

entries.definition: the science of matter and energy. Greek physika meant natural things; the plural became the name of the science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学。希腊语 physika 意为“自然之物”，其复数形式成了这门学科的名字。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a body. It comes through French from Latin physicus, keeping the bodily focus.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形状与结构。它经法语来自拉丁语 physicus，保留了“身体”这一重心。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. In medieval Latin physicus meant a healer of natural things, that is, the body.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。在中世纪拉丁语里，physicus 指治疗自然之物（即身体）的人。

entries.definition: the study of what lies beyond the physical. Meta- 'after, beyond' plus physics: the books that came after the physics books.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界之外的东西的学问。meta-“之后、超越”加 physics：排在物理学著作之后的那批书。

entries.definition: relating to the body. Bodily overlaps physical in sense 01 but has no material or scientific senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的。bodily 在第 1 义项上与 physical 重叠，但没有物质义或科学义。

entries.definition: made of matter, or concerned with possessions. Material fits sense 02; physical also covers the body and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 由物质构成的，或与财物有关的。material 对应第 2 义项；physical 还覆盖身体与物理学。

entries.definition: having a body. Corporeal is the formal word for sense 01 and is rarely used of objects.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有肉身的。corporeal 是第 1 义项的正式说法，很少用于物体。

entries.definition: able to be touched or clearly perceived. Tangible matches sense 04 and stresses the sense of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 能被触摸或清楚感知的。tangible 对应第 4 义项，强调触觉。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. Natural matches sense 06 and shares the same underlying idea of physis.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、非人造的。natural 对应第 6 义项，底层同样是 physis 的观念。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the body that can be touched, the material object, the physics lab, the printed book, and the sports field.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摸得到的身体、物质对象、物理实验室、印成书的实体、运动场上的对抗。

normal.en: Physical = what you can poke. If your finger stops at it, it is physical.
normal.cn: physical＝你能戳到的东西。手指停在上面的，就是 physical。

normal.en: Physis is nature, and your body is the piece of nature you carry around.
normal.cn: physis 是自然，而你的身体就是你随身携带的那块自然。

normal.en: Physics and physical are the same root: one is the science, the other is what the science studies.
normal.cn: physics 与 physical 同根：一个是学科，一个是这门学科研究的东西。

normal.en: A physical exam is literally a body check: the adjective became the name of the appointment.
normal.cn: a physical exam 字面就是“对身体做的检查”：形容词变成了那次预约的名字。

normal.en: Metaphysics sits after physics: meta- means after, so it is the study of what the physical cannot cover.
normal.cn: metaphysics 排在 physics 之后：meta- 意为“之后”，所以它研究 physical 覆盖不到的部分。

abstract.en: The physical is the layer that resists you; everything else is negotiation.
abstract.cn: 物理层就是会抵抗你的那一层；其余的一切都是协商。

abstract.en: Nature, body, matter, reality: one Greek word supplied four different borders for what counts as real.
abstract.cn: 自然、身体、物质、实在：一个希腊词为“什么算真实”划出了四道不同的边界。

abstract.en: To call something physical is to claim it can be measured; measurement is the modern form of the old word for nature.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 physical，就是声称它可以被测量；测量是那个古老的“自然”一词的现代形态。

examples.en: After the accident he needed months of physical therapy before he could walk unaided.
examples.cn: 事故之后他需要数月的物理治疗，才能独立行走。

examples.en: The two servers are physically separate even though they share one logical name.
examples.cn: 这两台服务器虽然共用一个逻辑名称，物理上是分开的。

examples.en: Detectives found physical evidence that contradicted the witness's account.
examples.cn: 警探找到了与证人陈述相矛盾的实物证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: “菲兹克”听起来像“非此刻”——不是此刻的想法，而是此刻摸得着的东西：physical 物质的、身体的

root: 希腊语 phyein“生长”→ physis“自然（生长之物）”→ physikos“自然的”→ 拉丁 physicus → 英语 physical；与 physics、physique、physician、metaphysics 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Everything here comes from one Greek word for nature. The body is nature closest to us; matter is nature outside us; physics is nature studied; a physical exam is the body inspected; physical evidence is reality that can be handled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这里的一切都出自一个表示“自然”的希腊词。身体是离我们最近的自然；物质是我们之外的自然；物理学是被研究的自然；体检是被检查的身体；实物证据是可以拿在手里的实在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing against a solid surface and feeling it push back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在坚实表面上，感到它顶回来。

branches.en: BODY: the natural self and the examination of it.
branches.cn: 身体：自然的自身，以及对它的检查。

branches.en: MATTER: material properties, tangible reality, and evidence that can be handled.
branches.cn: 物质：物质属性、可触摸的实在、可拿在手里的证据。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the department that studies matter and energy.
branches.cn: 科学：研究物质与能量的那门学科。

branches.en: FORCE: bodies in contact, effort and collision.
branches.cn: 力：身体相触，用力与碰撞。

branches.en: NATURE: the non-human world, kept closest to the Greek original.
branches.cn: 自然：非人造的世界，最贴近希腊原义。

intro.en: The family rests on the Greek noun for nature and its adjective. English adds the usual endings for sciences, persons, and properties.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语表示“自然”的名词及其形容词上。英语加上表示学科、人物与性质的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed physicus and physica, and through them the root reached medicine before it reached physics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入 physicus 与 physica，这条词根先进入医学，后才进入物理学。

items.meaningCN: 表示研究者或从业者的后缀

definition_zh: 政策；方针；原则；保险单；（古）治国术
definition_en: a course of action or set of principles adopted by a government or organization; a written contract of insurance
core_image: 一群人先定下走哪条路，再让所有人照这条路走
scene: The government announced a new policy on carbon emissions.
sceneCN: 这里 policy 是「政府采取的行动方针」（第 1 个义项：政策）；句意：政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。场景要点：公共决定、成文、要被执行。

derivatives.zh: 明智的；精明的（同 polis 线，但词义已分化）

senses.title: A government's course of action
senses.titleCN: 政策：政府选定的那条路
senses.definition: a course of action chosen by a government or a political party on a matter of public concern
senses.definitionCN: 政府或政党在公共事务上选定的行动路线
senses.example: The government announced a new policy on carbon emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 政府宣布了一项关于碳排放的新政策。
senses.why: Greek politeia meant the conduct of public affairs. A policy is that conduct made explicit: a line the state decides to follow.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 politeia 意为“公共事务的治理”。policy 就是把这种治理摆到明处：国家决定要走的一条线。

senses.title: A rule adopted by an organization
senses.titleCN: 制度：组织内部定下的规矩
senses.definition: an agreed set of rules or principles that guides decisions inside a company, school, or other body
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或其他机构内部为决策而议定的一套规则或原则
senses.example: Company policy forbids personal use of the printers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司制度禁止把打印机用于私人用途。
senses.why: The state's line of action scaled down to any institution. What a body decides to keep doing becomes its standing policy.
senses.whyCN: 把国家的行动路线缩到任何机构。一个组织决定长期这么做，就成了它固定的制度。

senses.title: A written contract of insurance
senses.titleCN: 保险单：那张写满条款的纸
senses.definition: the written document in which an insurer agrees to cover specified risks for a premium
senses.definitionCN: 保险人同意以保费为代价承保特定风险的书面文件
senses.example: Read the policy carefully before you sign it.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前要仔细读保险单。
senses.why: This is a different word in origin: Italian polizza meant a written note or proof. It came into English with the same spelling as the political word but from another root.
senses.whyCN: 这其实是另一个词源：意大利语 polizza 意为书面凭据或证明。它带着和政治义相同的拼写进入英语，但词根不同。

senses.title: Insurance cover in general
senses.titleCN: 保险：所买的保障本身
senses.definition: the protection bought under such a contract, spoken of as a thing one holds
senses.definitionCN: 依该合同获得的保障，被当作一件持有的东西来说
senses.example: The house is covered by a separate policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子另有一份保险。
senses.why: The paper stands for the protection it records. Holding the policy is holding the cover, so the word shifts from document to benefit.
senses.whyCN: 那张纸代表它所记录的保障。持有保单就是持有保障，于是词义从文件滑向利益。

senses.title: Archaic: statecraft
senses.titleCN: 古义：治国之术
senses.definition: the art or practice of managing a state, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 较古的用法，指治理国家的技艺或实践
senses.example: In Renaissance manuals, policy meant the craft of ruling well.
senses.exampleCN: 在文艺复兴时期的手册里，policy 指善于治国的技艺。
senses.why: This is the original sense from Greek politeia. It survives mainly in historical writing, where policy names the skill rather than one decision.
senses.whyCN: 这是来自希腊 politeia 的本义。它主要残存在历史叙述里，那里 policy 命名的是技能，而不是某一项决定。

senses.title: A party's declared programme
senses.titleCN: 政纲：政党公开的主张
senses.definition: the set of positions and plans that a political party puts forward
senses.definitionCN: 一个政党提出的一套立场与计划
senses.example: The party's education policy won support in the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的教育政策在城市赢得了支持。
senses.why: A party is a body that must state in advance what it will do. Its platform is policy in the form of a public promise.
senses.whyCN: 政党是一个必须事先说明将做什么的团体。它的政纲就是以公开承诺形式出现的政策。

senses.title: The field of public policy
senses.titleCN: 公共政策：研究怎么定的那门学问
senses.definition: the academic and professional study of how public decisions are made and evaluated
senses.definitionCN: 对公共决定如何作出与如何评估所作的学术与专业研究
senses.example: She studied public policy before joining the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她在进入部委之前学的是公共政策。
senses.why: Once policies are numerous and consequential, the making of them becomes an object of study, and the word names the field.
senses.whyCN: 当政策数量繁多且后果重大时，“制定政策”本身成了研究对象，这个词也就成了学科名。

senses.title: Expedient line of action
senses.titleCN: 权宜：为成事先这么办
senses.definition: a line of action chosen for practical advantage rather than for principle
senses.definitionCN: 为实际好处而非为原则选择的行动路线
senses.example: He called it policy, though everyone knew it was a delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他称之为策略，但谁都知道那只是拖延。
senses.why: When principle is absent, the chosen line is still a line. The word then carries a hint of calculated convenience.
senses.whyCN: 没有原则时，所选的那条线仍是一条线。此时这个词就带上了“精于算计的便利”的暗示。

intro.en: Policy is two unrelated words that ended up spelled alike. One comes from the Greek word for city and gave us politics. The other comes from a Greek word for proof and gave us the insurance document.
intro.cn: policy 是两个本不相关的词，最后拼成了一样。一个来自希腊语表示“城邦”的词，也就是 politics 那一线；另一个来自希腊语表示“证明”的词，即保险单那一线。

items.en: Polis meant 'city, city-state'. It is the base of politics, police, polity, and metropolis. Its own earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: polis 意为“城、城邦”。它是 politics、police、polity、metropolis 的基底。它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Politeia meant 'citizenship, the constitution, the conduct of public affairs'. It is polis plus the abstract noun ending -teia.
items.cn: politeia 意为“公民身份、政体、公共事务的治理”。它由 polis 加抽象名词词尾 -teia 构成。

items.en: Late Latin politia took the Greek word and used it for the ordering of a commonwealth. It is the direct parent of the political policy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 politia 接取了这个希腊词，用来指共同体的秩序。它正是政治义 policy 的直接父辈。

items.en: Old French policie meant 'government, administration, political organization'. English borrowed it in the late 14th century, first as statecraft and then as a specific course of action.
items.cn: 古法语 policie 意为“政府、行政、政治组织”。英语于 14 世纪后期借入，先指治国术，后指具体的行动方针。

items.en: The insurance word has a separate chain: Greek apodeixis 'proof, demonstration' (apo- 'from' + deiknynai 'to show') became Medieval Latin apodissa, then Italian polizza 'a written note or certificate', then French police, and English policy in the 1560s. The identity with the political word is only in spelling.
items.cn: 保险义有另一条独立的链：希腊语 apodeixis“证明、演示”（apo-“出自”+ deiknynai“显示”）→ 中世纪拉丁 apodissa → 意大利语 polizza“书面凭据或证书” → 法语 police → 英语 16 世纪 60 年代的 policy。它与政治义只在拼写上相同。

items.en: The two words now share one spelling. Context decides: public policy, company policy, and insurance policy are three different things, and only the first two belong to the polis family.
items.cn: 两个词如今共用一种拼写。靠语境分辨：public policy、company policy、insurance policy 是三件不同的事，只有前两者属于 polis 词族。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek city root, including the French form that also produced the insurance sense. The second group collects words for rules and plans.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊“城邦”词根，其中也含那个衍生出保险义的法语形式。第二组收表示规则与计划的词。

entries.definition: the activity of governing and competing for power. From Greek politikos 'of a citizen', from polis 'city'.
entries.definitionCN: 治理与争夺权力的活动。来自希腊语 politikos“公民的”，再往上为 polis“城邦”。

entries.definition: the body that enforces law. It goes back through French to Late Latin politia, the same polis family, but never means a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 执行法律的机构。它经法语回溯到晚期拉丁 politia，同属 polis 词族，但从不表示“政策”。

entries.definition: a politically organized society, or its form of government. It is the direct English descendant of Latin politia.
entries.definitionCN: 政治上有组织的社会，或其政体形式。它是拉丁 politia 的直接英语后裔。

entries.definition: the person who owns an insurance policy. It uses the insurance sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 持有保险单的人。它只使用保险义。

entries.definition: an overall plan for achieving a goal. Strategy is designed to win; policy is what an authority decides to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成目标所作的总体计划。strategy 为取胜而设计；policy 是权威决定要遵循的路线。

entries.definition: a stated instruction about what may be done. A rule is one item; a policy is the principle behind a set of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 关于可以做什么的明文规定。rule 是单独一条；policy 是一组规则背后的原则。

entries.definition: advice about how to act, usually not compulsory. Guidelines are softer than policy, which is binding within an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 关于如何行动的指导意见，通常不强制。guideline 比 policy 软，后者在组织内具有约束力。

entries.definition: the fixed steps for doing something. Procedure is about how; policy is about what and why.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的固定步骤。procedure 关乎怎么做；policy 关乎做什么和为什么。

entries.definition: a stated attitude toward an issue. A stance is where you stand; a policy is what you then do from there.
entries.definitionCN: 对某议题表明的态度。stance 是你站的位置；policy 是你从那里开始做的事。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the chosen road, the company handbook, the two word origins, the insurance paper, and the party platform.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：选定的路、公司手册、两个词源、保险那张纸、政党纲领。

normal.en: A policy is a road picked in advance. Once picked, everyone walks it.
normal.cn: policy 是提前选好的路。一旦选定，所有人都走这条。

normal.en: Company policy is the page in the handbook that answers what you are allowed to do.
normal.cn: company policy 就是手册里那一页，回答“你能做什么”。

normal.en: Two roots, one spelling: polis gives public policy, apodeixis gives insurance policy.
normal.cn: 两个词根，一种拼写：polis 给出公共政策，apodeixis 给出保险单。

normal.en: An insurance policy is a paper you keep in a drawer until the day you need it.
normal.cn: 保险单是你放在抽屉里、直到需要那天才拿出来的那张纸。

normal.en: A party's policy is a promise written before the election so it can be checked after.
normal.cn: 政党政策是选前写下的承诺，好让选后被核对。

abstract.en: A policy is a decision made once and then applied many times; its power lies in not being re-argued every morning.
abstract.cn: 政策是一次作出、多次适用的决定；它的力量在于不必每天早上重新争论。

abstract.en: Every policy draws a line between what a group will consider and what it will ignore.
abstract.cn: 每一项政策都在“群体会考虑什么”与“群体将忽略什么”之间划一条线。

abstract.en: Rules are visible; the policy behind them is the invisible shape that makes the rules fit together.
abstract.cn: 规则是看得见的；规则背后的政策，是让这些规则彼此契合的无形形状。

examples.en: The Fed changed its interest-rate policy after inflation slowed.
examples.cn: 通胀放缓后，美联储改变了利率政策。

examples.en: Under company policy, all visitors must sign in at reception.
examples.cn: 按公司制度，所有来访者都必须在接待处登记。

examples.en: Her life insurance policy names her brother as the beneficiary.
examples.cn: 她的人寿保险单指定她弟弟为受益人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破例色”要小心——政策（policy）一旦定下，就不能随便破例；不过保险单那一支跟这个谐音无关

root: 两支：①政治义：希腊 polis“城邦”→ politeia“公共治理”→ 拉丁 politia → 古法语 policie → 英语 policy（14 世纪末）；②保险义：希腊 apodeixis“证明”→ 中世纪拉丁 apodissa → 意大利 polizza → 法语 police → 英语 policy（1560s）。

sensesIntro.en: The political senses all describe a line an authority decides to follow, from a state's grand course down to one office's rules. The insurance senses came from a different Greek word and only borrowed the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 政治义的各个义项都描述权威决定要遵循的一条线，从国家的大政到单个办公室的规矩。保险义来自另一个希腊词，只借用了拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group agreeing on one road before anyone starts walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人在动身之前先议定只走一条路。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: what a government or party decides to do.
branches.cn: 公共路线：政府或政党决定要做的事。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: rules inside a body, and the study of how such decisions are made.
branches.cn: 机构：团体内部的规则，以及研究这类决定如何作出的学问。

branches.en: CRAFT: the older sense, governing as a skill rather than as one decision.
branches.cn: 技艺：较古的义项，把治理看成技能而非某一项决定。

branches.en: EXPEDIENCY: a line chosen for advantage, which is policy without principle.
branches.cn: 权宜：为利益选择的路线，即没有原则的政策。

branches.en: INSURANCE: a separate word, the document and the cover it represents.
branches.cn: 保险：另一个词，指文件以及它所代表的保障。

intro.en: The political family is built on the Greek word for city. The insurance word belongs to a completely different set of pieces, which is why mixing them is a common error.
intro.cn: 政治义词族建立在希腊语“城邦”一词上。保险义属于完全不同的一套构件，所以把两者混为一谈是常见错误。

latinIntro.en: Latin politia carried the city root into French and English; apodissa carried the proof root into Italian and then French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 politia 把“城邦”词根带进法语和英语；apodissa 则把“证明”词根带进意大利语，再进法语。

items.exampleCN: 证明（保险义的最早源头）

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或动作的名词后缀
