definition_zh: 部分；一份（食物）；应得的份额；命运；（动词）分配
definition_en: a part or share of something larger; an amount of food served to one person; to divide something into shares
core_image: 把一整块切开，把属于你的那一份放到你面前
scene: Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
sceneCN: 这里 portion 是「分给一个人的一份食物」（第 2 个义项：一份）；句意：每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。场景要点：整块被切开、按人分、放在各自盘里。

collocations.zh: 最大的一份（源自狮子分猎物的典故）

derivatives.zh: 没有份额的；无嫁妆的（古）

senses.title: A part of a whole
senses.titleCN: 部分：整体里的一块
senses.definition: a part of a larger whole, especially one separated or regarded separately
senses.definitionCN: 一个更大整体中的一部分，尤指被分开或单独看待的那部分
senses.example: A large portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中很大一部分用于工资。
senses.why: Latin portio meant a share assigned to someone. The word begins with the act of cutting a whole and handing out pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 portio 意为“分派给某人的一份”。这个词起于这样一个动作：把整体切开，再把块分出去。

senses.title: A serving of food
senses.titleCN: 一份（食物）：放到你盘里的量
senses.definition: the amount of food served to one person at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次盛给一个人的食物量
senses.example: Each guest received a generous portion of the roast.
senses.exampleCN: 每位客人都分到了一份量很足的烤肉。
senses.why: Food is the most everyday whole that gets divided. The share on your plate is a portion in the most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 食物是最日常的被分割的整体。你盘里的那一份，就是最具体的 portion。

senses.title: An allotted share of property
senses.titleCN: 应得份额：法律上分给你的那一份
senses.definition: the share of an estate or property that is assigned to a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 遗产或财产中分配给某个特定人的份额
senses.example: She received her portion of the family land at twenty-one.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十一岁时得到了属于自己的那份家族土地。
senses.why: Inheritance makes the metaphor legal: the whole is fixed, the shares are named, and each heir gets a portion.
senses.whyCN: 继承把这个比喻法律化了：整体是固定的，份额是有名分的，每个继承人各得一份。

senses.title: One's lot or fate
senses.titleCN: 命运：分给一生的那一份
senses.definition: the share of life, good or bad, that a person is given, in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，指一个人被分得的那一份人生，无论好坏
senses.example: He accepted his portion of suffering without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了分给自己的那份苦难。
senses.why: If goods can be allotted, so can experiences. Life itself becomes a whole divided among people, and yours is your portion.
senses.whyCN: 如果财物可以被分派，经历也可以。人生本身成了一个分给众人的整体，你的那一份就是你的 portion。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.titleCN: 分配：把整块切成份
senses.definition: to divide something into shares and give them out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份并发给各人
senses.example: The committee portioned the funds among the three projects.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会把资金分给了三个项目。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act that produced it: to portion is to perform the cutting and handing out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成产生它的那个动作：to portion 就是执行“切开并分发”这件事。

senses.title: To provide with a dowry
senses.titleCN: 给嫁妆：旧时按份给女儿财产
senses.definition: in older usage, to give a daughter a dowry or a share of property at marriage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指在女儿出嫁时给她嫁妆或一份财产
senses.example: The will portioned his daughters before his sons.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱先给女儿们分好了嫁妆，然后才轮到儿子。
senses.why: A dowry is literally a daughter's portion, the share set aside for her. The verb records that legal practice.
senses.whyCN: 嫁妆字面就是“女儿的那一份”，即为她单留出来的份额。动词记录的就是这一法律习俗。

senses.title: A section of a larger work
senses.titleCN: 章节：一部作品里的一段
senses.definition: one section of a book, document, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书、文件或乐曲中的一个段落
senses.example: Only a small portion of the report deals with costs.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里只有一小部分谈到成本。
senses.why: A text is a whole too. It can be divided into sections, and each section is a portion of the text.
senses.whyCN: 文本也是一个整体，可以被分成段落，每一段就是文本的一个 portion。

senses.title: An allocated amount
senses.titleCN: 配额：按规定量给你的数
senses.definition: a measured amount of something allocated to a person or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按定量分配给某人或某用途的一份数量
senses.example: The daily portion of grain was weighed out at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 每天那份谷物在黎明时称好分出。
senses.why: When the share is measured rather than simply cut, portion means a fixed quantity: a ration by another name.
senses.whyCN: 当份额是被量出来的而不只是切出来的，portion 就指一个固定数量：换个名字的配给量。

intro.en: Portion comes from a Latin word for an assigned share. The step before it rests on a reconstructed form, so that link is probable rather than directly recorded.
intro.cn: portion 来自拉丁语中表示“分派的份额”的词。它前面的一步建立在重构形式上，因此那一环是“很可能”，而非有直接文献记录。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, a part, an allotted portion'. It is recorded in classical Latin for shares of property and of food.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、部分、分得的一份”。古典拉丁语中已用它指财产与食物的份额。

items.en: Portio is generally traced to a reconstructed *partio 'division', related to pars 'part' and ultimately to PIE *pere- (2) 'to grant, allot'. The asterisk marks a form found in no text, so this link is probable rather than documented.
items.cn: portio 一般被追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，并可再上溯到原始印欧语 *pere- (2)“分配、给予”。星号表示这个形式不见于任何文献，所以这一环是“很可能”，而非有据可查。

items.en: Old French took the Latin accusative portionem and shaped it as porcion, meaning a share or a part.
items.cn: 古法语取拉丁语宾格 portionem，改造为 porcion，意为一份或一部分。

items.en: English borrowed porcion in the early 14th century. Early uses are legal and religious: a share of an estate, a share of goods, an assigned lot in life.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪初借入 porcion。早期用法多属法律与宗教：遗产的一份、财物的一份、被分得的人生际遇。

items.en: The everyday sense 'amount of food for one person' develops later and becomes dominant in modern usage, especially in restaurants and diet advice.
items.cn: “一人份食物量”这一日常义发展较晚，却在现代用法中占据主导，尤其在餐饮与饮食建议里。

items.en: The verb appears alongside the noun, and compounds such as apportion and proportion extend the family. All of them keep the picture of cutting a whole into shares.
items.cn: 动词与名词并行出现，apportion、proportion 等复合词扩展了这个词族。它们都保留了“把整体切成份”的画面。

note.en: The first group is built by adding prefixes to portion itself. The second group collects words for parts and shares.
note.cn: 第一组是在 portion 本身前面加前缀构成。第二组收表示“部分与份额”的词。

entries.definition: to divide and assign in due shares. Ad- 'to' plus portion: to give each their portion.
entries.definitionCN: 按应得的份额划分并分配。ad-“向”加 portion：给每个人应得的那一份。

entries.definition: a relation between parts, or a balanced share. Pro- 'in relation to' plus portion gives the idea of shares measured against each other.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间的关系，或均衡的份额。pro-“相对”加 portion，给出“份额互相比量”的意思。

entries.definition: changing in a fixed ratio with something else. It extends proportion with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一事物按固定比率变化的。它由 proportion 加 -al 扩展而来。

entries.definition: having no share, especially no dowry. Portion plus -less, common in older legal and literary texts.
entries.definitionCN: 没有份额的，尤指没有嫁妆。portion 加 -less，多见于较早的法律与文学文本。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. Part is the broad neutral word; portion adds the idea of a share assigned to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一块。part 是宽泛中性的词；portion 多出“分配给某人的份额”之意。

entries.definition: a part belonging to or owed to a person. Share matches portion in legal and financial contexts and is more common there.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某人或应归某人的一部分。share 在法律与财务语境中与 portion 相当，且更常用。

entries.definition: an amount of food for one person. Serving is the everyday restaurant word; portion also carries the sense of an allotted share.
entries.definitionCN: 供一个人吃的食物量。serving 是餐馆日常用语；portion 还带有“分得的份额”之意。

entries.definition: an amount officially given out. Allotment stresses official distribution; portion can be informal or literary.
entries.definitionCN: 官方分发的数量。allotment 强调官方分配；portion 可以是非正式的或文学性的。

entries.definition: a fixed allowance of something scarce. Ration implies shortage and control; portion does not.
entries.definitionCN: 对稀缺物资的固定配给量。ration 含短缺与管制之意；portion 不含。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the slice on the plate, the inheritance, the measured grain, the prefix family, and the fate you are dealt.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：盘里的那一块、遗产里的那一份、量出来的谷物、前缀家族、分给你的一生。

normal.en: Picture a whole roast cut into slices. The slice on your plate is your portion.
normal.cn: 想象一整块烤肉被切成片。你盘里的那一片就是你的 portion。

normal.en: Portion out means hand each person their slice, one by one.
normal.cn: portion out 就是一片一片地把属于各人的那份递过去。

normal.en: In a will, the whole estate is divided and each child gets a portion.
normal.cn: 遗嘱里，整份遗产被切开，每个孩子得到一份 portion。

normal.en: A portion of grain weighed at dawn is a ration under another name.
normal.cn: 黎明时称出的那份谷物，就是换个名字的配给量。

normal.en: Apportion, proportion, portionless: same core, different prefixes and suffixes.
normal.cn: apportion、proportion、portionless：同一个核心，不同的前后缀。

abstract.en: Every whole can be cut, and every cut produces an owner; portion is the word where division becomes possession.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可被切开，每次切开都产生一个所有者；portion 正是“分割变成占有”的那个词。

abstract.en: A portion is a boundary drawn inside a thing, and boundaries are always drawn by someone.
abstract.cn: 一份是在事物内部画出的一条界线，而界线总是由某个人画的。

abstract.en: When life is called a portion, the metaphor admits that not everything is available to everyone.
abstract.cn: 当人生被称为一份 portion 时，这个比喻承认了：并非所有东西对所有人都是可得的。

examples.en: Only a small portion of the manuscript has survived.
examples.cn: 这份手稿只有一小部分留存下来。

examples.en: Restaurants here are known for generous portions at low prices.
examples.cn: 这里的餐馆以分量足、价格低闻名。

examples.en: The land was portioned among the villagers after the reform.
examples.cn: 改革之后，土地被分给了村民。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖心”——把整颗心剖开，分给每人一份，就是 portion（份额）；注意这只是谐音，与词源无关

root: 拉丁语 portio“份额、部分”（一般追溯到重构形式 *partio“划分”，与 pars“部分”相关，来自 PIE *pere- (2)“分配”）→ 古法语 porcion → 英语 portion（14 世纪初）。

sensesIntro.en: The word always involves cutting a whole and assigning a piece. Food, inheritance, text, and even fate are all wholes of different kinds, and the piece assigned to you is your portion. The verb simply performs that cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终涉及“把整体切开并指派一块”。食物、遗产、文本乃至命运，都是不同种类的整体，分给你的那一块就是你的 portion。动词则是执行这一刀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole loaf cut at the table, one slice placed before each person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整条面包在桌上被切开，每个面前放上一片。

chain: A PART CUT FROM A WHOLE

branches.en: PART: a piece of any whole, whether a budget or a book.
branches.cn: 部分：任何整体中的一块，无论是预算还是书。

branches.en: MEASURE: the plate and the scale, food and fixed allowance.
branches.cn: 量：盘子与秤，食物与定量。

branches.en: LAW: inheritance shares and the dowry set aside for a daughter.
branches.cn: 法律：继承份额与为女儿单留的嫁妆。

branches.en: FATE: the share of life dealt to a person.
branches.cn: 命运：分给一个人的那份人生。

branches.en: ACTION: the act of cutting and handing out.
branches.cn: 动作：切开并分发的行为。

intro.en: Portion has generated a small family through prefixes that specify direction or relation (to, for, in ratio) and suffixes that make adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: portion 通过表示方向或关系的前缀（向、为、按比例）以及构成形容词与动词的后缀，衍生出一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun portio and its related verb forms supplied the base; English built the rest with native endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 portio 及其相关动词形式提供了基底；其余部分由英语用本土词尾构造。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 分配者（苏格兰法律用语）

items.meaningCN: 部分（与 portio 关系未证实）

definition_zh: 造成（问题、威胁）；提出（问题）；摆姿势；冒充；放置；（名词）姿势；装出的样子
definition_en: to create a problem or threat; to ask a question; to hold a body position; to pretend to be something; (noun) a posture or a pretence
core_image: 把一件东西摆到台面上，让所有人都看见它在那儿
scene: The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
sceneCN: 这里 pose 是「造成、摆出（问题）」（第 1 个义项）；句意：新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。场景要点：问题被摆到台面上、无法回避。

derivatives.zh: 摆姿势的人；难题（英式口语 a poser）
装腔作势的人（经法语回流）
休息；安放（与 pose 同出 pausare 一线）

senses.title: To create a problem or difficulty
senses.titleCN: 造成：把问题摆到台面上
senses.definition: to create a problem, difficulty, or risk that others must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 造成别人必须应对的问题、困难或风险
senses.example: The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense is to place something down. A problem that is posed is set in front of everyone, where it cannot be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具体义是“放置”。被 pose 出来的问题，就是被摆到所有人面前、再也无法忽略的问题。

senses.title: To ask a question
senses.titleCN: 提出：把问题摆到对方面前
senses.definition: to put a question to someone, especially in a formal or public setting
senses.definitionCN: 向某人提出问题，尤指在正式或公开场合
senses.example: Reporters posed several questions about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就延期一事提出了几个问题。
senses.why: A question is placed before the person who must answer it. The same gesture of setting something down, now verbal.
senses.whyCN: 问题被放到必须作答的人面前。还是同一个“把东西放下”的动作，只是换成了言辞。

senses.title: To pretend to be something
senses.titleCN: 冒充：把自己摆成另一个身份
senses.definition: to claim or pretend to be a particular person or type of person
senses.definitionCN: 声称或假装自己是某个特定的人或某类人
senses.example: He posed as a security guard to get into the building.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒充保安进入了那栋楼。
senses.why: A pretender arranges his appearance in front of others, the way an object is placed for display. The identity is worn like a staged position.
senses.whyCN: 冒充者把自己的外观摆到别人眼前，就像把物件摆出来展示。身份被当成一个摆好的位置穿戴起来。

senses.title: To hold a body position
senses.titleCN: 摆姿势：把身体摆成一个造型
senses.definition: to hold one's body in a particular position, especially for a portrait or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 让身体保持某个特定姿势，尤指为了画像或拍照
senses.example: She posed for the portrait with one hand on the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 她一只手扶着椅子，为这幅肖像摆好姿势。
senses.why: Here the body itself is the object being placed. The painter arranges the sitter the way one arranges a still-life.
senses.whyCN: 这里被摆放的对象是身体本身。画家安排坐像的姿态，就像安排一组静物。

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.titleCN: 放置：把东西摆到某处
senses.definition: to put or place something in a position, in formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到某个位置，用于正式或文学语体
senses.example: He posed the vase on the windowsill and stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 他把花瓶放到窗台上，然后退后一步。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, the one from which every figurative sense borrows its picture.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的本义，所有引申义都是从这里借走那幅画面。

senses.title: Noun: a posture or attitude
senses.titleCN: 名词：姿势、姿态
senses.definition: a particular position of the body, or a way of behaving that is held for others to see
senses.definitionCN: 身体的某个特定姿势，或为了给别人看而保持的一种行为方式
senses.example: He struck a relaxed pose against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠在墙上，摆出一个放松的姿态。
senses.why: The verb's product becomes a noun: the position that has been placed and is now held.
senses.whyCN: 动词的产物变成名词：那个被摆好、并正在保持的位置。

senses.title: Noun: an affected manner
senses.titleCN: 名词：装出来的样子
senses.definition: a way of behaving that is adopted to impress others and is not sincere
senses.definitionCN: 为了给别人留下印象而采用、并不真诚的行为方式
senses.example: His indifference was only a pose.
senses.exampleCN: 他的漠不关心只是装出来的。
senses.why: If a posture is deliberately arranged, it can also be a false one. The visible position no longer matches the inner state.
senses.whyCN: 既然姿态是被刻意安排出来的，它也就可以是假的。可见的位置不再与内在状态相符。

senses.title: To constitute a threat
senses.titleCN: 构成：把威胁摆到面前
senses.definition: to be a danger or menace to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物构成危险或威胁
senses.example: The invasive species poses a threat to native birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种入侵物种对本地鸟类构成威胁。
senses.why: A threat is a problem aimed at someone. It is placed in their path, the same way an obstacle is placed on a road.
senses.whyCN: 威胁是冲着某人来的问题。它被摆到对方的路上，就像障碍被摆在道路中央。

intro.en: Pose came into English from French with the sense of placing. Its family history is tangled: a Latin verb meaning to pause lies behind it, while a different Latin verb meaning to place reshaped it.
intro.cn: pose 从法语进入英语，带着“放置”的意思。它的家族史相当缠绕：背后是一个意为“停顿”的拉丁动词，而另一个意为“放置”的拉丁动词又改造了它。

items.en: The French verb poser is generally traced to Vulgar Latin *pausare 'to halt, to rest', the same source as English pause and repose. The asterisk marks a reconstructed form, not a recorded one.
items.cn: 法语动词 poser 一般被追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”，与英语 pause、repose 同源。星号表示这是重构形式，并非文献中实际记录的词。

items.en: Old French poser meant 'to put, place, set', and also 'to propose', especially in debating. Its placement sense is explained in the next item.
items.cn: 古法语 poser 意为“放、置、摆”，也指“提议”，尤用于辩论场合。其中“放置”义的来由见下一项。

items.en: Latin ponere, past participle positus, means 'to put, place', and its participle is the source of position, positive, deposit, and compose. Old French poser was not derived from it; rather, the similar stems were confused, and poser took over the 'place' sense. This is a documented case of confusion, not a shared root.
items.cn: 拉丁 ponere（过去分词 positus）意为“放置”，其分词是 position、positive、deposit、compose 的来源。古法语 poser 并非由它派生；真实情况是两个词干相似而被混同，poser 于是接管了“放置”义。这是有文献记载的混同，而非同源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 14th century. Early senses include 'to suppose, to put forward', which survives in the phrase to pose a question.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个动词。早期义包括“设想、提出”，这层意思残存在 to pose a question 这一说法里。

items.en: The sense 'to hold a position for a portrait' develops later, and the noun pose, meaning a posture, is recorded in the early 19th century.
items.cn: “为画像保持某个姿势”的义项发展较晚；名词 pose（姿势）记录于 19 世纪初。

items.en: Modern English keeps both branches: placing (pose a question, pose a threat) and posturing (pose for a photo, a false pose). They meet in the same image of something set before the eyes.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两支：放置（pose a question、pose a threat）与摆姿态（pose for a photo、a false pose）。两者汇合于同一个画面：某物被摆到眼前。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for placing, which is the hidden root behind much of this family. The second group collects verbs of putting forward and showing off.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“放置”的动词，它是这个词族背后隐藏的根。第二组收表示“提出”与“摆样子”的动词。

entries.definition: the place where something is, or a point of view. From Latin positio, from positus, the participle of ponere 'to place'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所在的地点，或一种观点。来自拉丁 positio，再往上为 ponere“放置”的分词 positus。

entries.definition: the way the body is held. From Latin positura, also from ponere, and it overlaps with pose in the bodily sense.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的持姿方式。来自拉丁 positura，同样出自 ponere，在身体义上与 pose 重叠。

entries.definition: to put together, or to calm oneself. Com- 'together' plus ponere 'place': to place things together.
entries.definitionCN: 组合而成，或使镇定。com-“一起”加 ponere“放置”：把东西放在一起。

entries.definition: to put down, or money placed in a bank. De- 'down' plus positus: something placed down.
entries.definitionCN: 放下，或存入银行的钱。de-“向下”加 positus：被放下的东西。

entries.definition: to put something forward for consideration. Present is neutral and formal; pose often implies a difficulty or a challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事提交考虑。present 中性而正式；pose 常含“造成困难或挑战”之意。

entries.definition: to bring up a question or issue. Raise is the common verb for questions; pose is slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 提出一个问题或议题。raise 是提问题的常用动词；pose 稍正式。

entries.definition: to act as if something is true. Pretend is broader; pose as means adopt a false identity.
entries.definitionCN: 表现得好像某事为真。pretend 更宽；pose as 指冒充某个身份。

entries.definition: a deliberate bodily attitude, often used figuratively for political positioning. Posture is the more formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 有意摆出的身体姿态，也常比喻政治上的站位。posture 是更正式的名词。

entries.definition: to put something in a position. Place is the plain everyday verb; pose in this sense is literary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在某个位置。place 是日常平实的动词；pose 的这个义项带文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the object placed on the table, the question put to you, the fake uniform, the painter's sitter, and the borrowed pose.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摆上桌的物件、推到你面前的问题、假制服、画家的模特、借来的姿态。

normal.en: Pose = place. Whatever is posed is put in front of you and stays there.
normal.cn: pose＝放置。凡被 pose 出来的，都摆在你面前，并且留在那儿。

normal.en: Pose a question: the question is physically set down between you and the person who must answer.
normal.cn: pose a question：问题被实打实地放在你和必须作答的人中间。

normal.en: Pose as a guard: you wear an identity the way you wear a uniform.
normal.cn: pose as a guard：你把身份穿在身上，就像穿上一套制服。

normal.en: Pose for a portrait: your body becomes the still-life the painter arranges.
normal.cn: pose for a portrait：你的身体成了画家摆布的那组静物。

normal.en: A pose can be sincere posture or a fake one; the noun covers both the stance and the act.
normal.cn: a pose 可以是真诚的姿态，也可以是假装的；这个名词同时覆盖“站姿”与“做戏”。

abstract.en: To pose a problem is to give it a location; what has no place can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 把问题 pose 出来，就是给它一个位置；没有位置的东西才能被忽略。

abstract.en: Every pose is a claim about where the body ends and the performance begins.
abstract.cn: 每一个姿态都在主张一件事：身体在哪里结束，表演从哪里开始。

abstract.en: The same gesture that sets a vase on a sill sets a question before a mind; placement is the common grammar of matter and speech.
abstract.cn: 把花瓶放上窗台与把问题放到心智面前，是同一个动作；放置是物质与言语共有的语法。

examples.en: The question posed by the audience was harder than any the professor had prepared for.
examples.cn: 听众提出的问题，比教授准备的任何一个都难。

examples.en: The model posed in silence while the students drew her.
examples.cn: 模特静静地摆着姿势，学生们画她。

examples.en: An empty warehouse poses no immediate danger, but it attracts trespassers.
examples.cn: 空仓库本身不构成直接危险，却会招来擅自进入的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖姿”——把姿势剖开摆给众人看，就是 pose（摆姿势）；问题被摆出来，也叫 pose

root: 古法语 poser“放、置、提出”，一般追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”（pause、repose 同源），其“放置”义很可能受拉丁 ponere／positum“放置”影响；英语 14 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a version of placing: a problem placed before people, a question placed before an answerer, a body placed for a painter, an identity placed over one's own. The noun is the position that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是“放置”的一个版本：问题被放到众人面前，疑问被放到作答者面前，身体被摆给画家，身份被罩在自己身上。名词则是放置后形成的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands setting an object down where everyone can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西放下，放在所有人都看得见的地方。

chain: A PROBLEM OR QUESTION PUT FORTH

branches.en: BURDEN: a problem or threat placed in someone's path.
branches.cn: 负担：被摆到某人路上的问题或威胁。

branches.en: SPEECH: a question placed before the one who must answer.
branches.cn: 言语：被放到作答者面前的问题。

branches.en: FALSE FRONT: an identity or attitude arranged for others to see.
branches.cn: 假面：为给别人看而安排好的身份或态度。

branches.en: BODY: the sitter's position and the resulting posture.
branches.cn: 身体：模特的姿势与由此形成的体态。

branches.en: PLACEMENT: the literal act of putting an object somewhere.
branches.cn: 放置：把物件放到某处的字面动作。

intro.en: Pose sits at the meeting point of two Latin families: the pause family from *pausare, and the place family from ponere. English endings then built nouns and agents.
intro.cn: pose 处在两个拉丁词族的交汇处：来自 *pausare 的“停顿”族，以及来自 ponere 的“放置”族。英语词尾再构造出名词与施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere and its participle positus supplied the place vocabulary; Vulgar Latin *pausare supplied the rest and resting vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere 及其分词 positus 提供了“放置”词汇；通俗拉丁 *pausare 提供了“休息、停驻”词汇。

definition_zh: 积极的；肯定的；正面的；确凿的；阳性的；正的；正电的；原级
definition_en: optimistic or hopeful; expressing agreement or certainty; showing that something is present; (of a number or charge) above zero
core_image: 在一张横轴上，站在零点右边，并明确说「是」
scene: She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
sceneCN: 这里 positive 是「心态积极的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。场景要点：方向朝上、向前看、不垮。

pos.zh: 积极的；肯定的；确凿的；阳性的；正的
正面之处；正数；（摄影）正片

derivatives.zh: 实证主义（只承认可观察事实）
假定；提出（与 positive 同出 positus）

senses.title: Optimistic and hopeful
senses.titleCN: 积极的：朝好处看的那种劲头
senses.definition: expecting good things and focusing on what can go well
senses.definitionCN: 期待好事、把注意力放在能顺利之处
senses.example: She stayed positive even after the third rejection.
senses.exampleCN: 即使被拒三次，她仍然保持积极。
senses.why: The word's core is 'laid down, definite'. A positive mind is one that has settled on the good outcome rather than leaving it open.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是“被确定下来”。积极的心态，就是把结果定在好处上，而不是让它悬着。

senses.title: Expressing agreement or yes
senses.titleCN: 肯定的：明确说「是」
senses.definition: expressing agreement, approval, or an affirmative answer
senses.definitionCN: 表达同意、赞许或肯定回答
senses.example: We received a positive reply within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一天之内就收到了肯定的答复。
senses.why: A positive answer is one that has been fixed: not maybe, not pending, but settled in the affirmative.
senses.whyCN: 肯定的回答是被固定下来的回答：不是也许，不是待定，而是定在“是”这一边。

senses.title: Good or beneficial in effect
senses.titleCN: 正面的：带来好结果的那一面
senses.definition: producing a good or useful effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生良好或有用的效果
senses.example: The new bus route had a positive impact on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新公交线路对本地商铺产生了正面影响。
senses.why: What is settled and real tends to be counted on the good side. Positive becomes the label for effects we want more of.
senses.whyCN: 被确定、被落实的东西往往被算在好的一边。positive 成了“我们希望更多”的效果的标签。

senses.title: Definite and undeniable
senses.titleCN: 确凿的：摆在那里，不容否认
senses.definition: clear, definite, and not open to doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、确定、不容怀疑
senses.example: We have positive proof that the letter was forged.
senses.exampleCN: 我们有确凿证据证明这封信是伪造的。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: in law, positive meant formally laid down. What is laid down is not a matter of opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：在法律上，positive 指正式规定下来的。被规定下来的，就不是意见问题。

senses.title: Medical: showing the condition is present
senses.titleCN: 阳性的：查出了那个东西
senses.definition: showing that a particular substance, infection, or condition is present in a test
senses.definitionCN: 表示在检测中发现某种物质、感染或状况确实存在
senses.example: He tested positive for the virus but had no symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病毒检测呈阳性，但没有症状。
senses.why: A test is a yes-or-no question put to the body. Positive means the thing asked about is definitely there, not absent.
senses.whyCN: 检测是向身体提出的一个是非题。positive 表示所问之物确实存在，而非缺席。

senses.title: Mathematics: above zero
senses.titleCN: 正的：在零点右边的数
senses.definition: of a number, greater than zero
senses.definitionCN: 指数值大于零
senses.example: Multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive result.
senses.exampleCN: 两个负数相乘得到正数结果。
senses.why: On a number line, positive marks the direction that counts upward from zero. The sign is a settled direction.
senses.whyCN: 在数轴上，正号标记从零点向上计数的方向。这个符号是一个确定下来的方向。

senses.title: Physics: carrying positive charge
senses.titleCN: 正电的：与电子相反的那种电荷
senses.definition: having the kind of electric charge carried by protons, opposite to that of electrons
senses.definitionCN: 带有质子所携的那种电荷，与电子所带电荷相反
senses.example: The positive terminal is marked with a plus sign.
senses.exampleCN: 正极用加号标出。
senses.why: Franklin's convention named one kind of charge positive, and the label stuck. It is a naming decision, not a claim about which charge is better.
senses.whyCN: 富兰克林的约定把其中一种电荷命名为 positive，这个叫法沿用至今。它是命名决定，并不表示哪种电荷“更好”。

senses.title: Grammar: the base degree
senses.titleCN: 语法：原级（不加比较）
senses.definition: in grammar, the simple form of an adjective or adverb, before comparison
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指形容词或副词未作比较的简单形式
senses.example: Good is the positive degree; better and best are the comparative and superlative.
senses.exampleCN: good 是原级；better 与 best 分别是比较级和最高级。
senses.why: The base form states a quality outright, with nothing added. It is the form laid down before any comparison modifies it.
senses.whyCN: 原级直接陈述一种性质，不加任何东西。它是任何比较来改动之前就已定下的形式。

intro.en: Positive comes from a Latin adjective meaning 'settled by agreement'. Its history runs from law to logic to mathematics to electricity, and only recently to optimism.
intro.cn: positive 来自一个意为“经约定确定下来”的拉丁形容词。它的历史从法律走到逻辑、数学、电学，而“乐观”这一义其实很晚才出现。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place'. Its past participle positus, 'placed, set down', is the stem of the whole family: position, deposit, compose, positive.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放置”。其过去分词 positus“被放置的、被定下的”，是整个词族的词干：position、deposit、compose、positive。

items.en: Positivus meant 'settled by agreement, conventional'. In medieval law it described rules laid down by authority, as opposed to natural law.
items.cn: positivus 意为“经约定确定的、约定俗成的”。在中世纪法律中，它指由权威制定下来的规则，与自然法相对。

items.en: English positive appears in the 14th century first in legal and philosophical writing, with the sense 'formally laid down, absolute'.
items.cn: 英语 positive 于 14 世纪出现，最早见于法律与哲学写作，意为“正式规定的、绝对的”。

items.en: By the 15th and 16th centuries it means 'definite, not open to doubt', and it also enters grammar for the uncompared degree of an adjective.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，它表示“确定的、不容怀疑”，并进入语法，指形容词未作比较的原级。

items.en: From the 18th century the word labels the direction above zero and, after Franklin, the kind of electric charge called positive. Photography later adds the positive image.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词标记零点以上的方向；在富兰克林之后，又标记被称为正的那种电荷。摄影随后又加上“正片”。

items.en: The everyday sense 'hopeful, optimistic' is a 20th-century development. It is the newest layer and is not found in the older legal or scientific uses.
items.cn: “充满希望、乐观”的日常义是 20 世纪的产物。它是最新的一层，在较早的法律或科学用法中找不到。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin participle. The second group collects words for approval, certainty, and good effect.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个拉丁分词上。第二组收表示赞同、确定与良好效果的词。

entries.definition: in a positive way, or absolutely. It also serves as an intensifier: positively dangerous means definitely dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 以积极的方式，或绝对地。它也用作强调词：positively dangerous 意为“绝对危险”。

entries.definition: to suggest or assume something as a fact. It comes from Latin positus, the same participle behind positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提出或假定某事为事实。它来自拉丁 positus，即 positive 背后的同一个分词。

entries.definition: a place or a point of view. From positio, a noun built on the same participle positus.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或观点。来自 positio，由同一个分词 positus 构成的名词。

entries.definition: the antiparticle of the electron, with positive charge. Formed in the 1930s from positive plus electron.
entries.definitionCN: 电子的反粒子，带正电。20 世纪 30 年代由 positive 与 electron 拼合而成。

entries.definition: expecting good outcomes. Optimistic is narrower than positive, which also covers agreement, proof, and electric charge.
entries.definitionCN: 期待好结果。optimistic 比 positive 窄，后者还覆盖赞同、证据与电荷。

entries.definition: saying yes or giving support. Affirmative matches sense 02 and is the formal opposite of negative.
entries.definitionCN: 说“是”或给予支持。affirmative 对应第 2 义项，是 negative 的正式反义。

entries.definition: sure about oneself or an outcome. Confident describes the feeling; positive can describe both the feeling and the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或结果有把握。confident 描述感受；positive 既可指感受，也可指证据。

entries.definition: helpful and intended to improve something. Constructive fits sense 03 and stresses usefulness rather than mood.
entries.definitionCN: 有益且意在改进的。constructive 对应第 3 义项，强调有用性而非情绪。

entries.definition: clear and certain. Definite matches sense 04 and is close to the older core of positive.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而确定的。definite 对应第 4 义项，贴近 positive 较古老的核心义。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the plus side of the axis, the firm yes, the proof on the table, the test result, and the uncompared adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：轴的正侧、干脆的“是”、桌上的证据、化验结果、未作比较的形容词。

normal.en: Positive is the plus side: on a number line it points right, and in mood it points up.
normal.cn: positive 是加号那一边：在数轴上指向右，在心情上指向上。

normal.en: A positive answer is a yes that has been nailed down, not a maybe.
normal.cn: 肯定的答复是被钉死的“是”，不是“也许”。

normal.en: Positive proof is evidence placed on the table where nobody can talk it away.
normal.cn: 确凿证据就是摆到桌上、谁也说不掉的证据。

normal.en: A positive test means the thing you asked about is definitely there, like a light turning on.
normal.cn: 阳性检测意味着你问的那个东西确实在，就像一盏灯亮了。

normal.en: In grammar the positive degree is the plain form before any comparison touches it.
normal.cn: 语法上的原级，就是任何比较来碰它之前的朴素形式。

abstract.en: Positive originally meant settled by authority, not cheerful; the modern smile is a late guest in an old legal house.
abstract.cn: positive 本指“由权威定下”，并非“愉快”；现代的笑脸是这座古老法律宅子里晚来的客人。

abstract.en: A plus sign is a decision about direction, not a discovery about value.
abstract.cn: 加号是关于方向的决定，而不是关于价值的发现。

abstract.en: To call evidence positive is to say the question is closed; that is why the word can sound both reassuring and dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把证据称为 positive，等于宣布问题已经关闭；所以这个词听上去既可让人安心，也可让人警觉。

examples.en: The study found a positive correlation between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 这项研究发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在正相关。

examples.en: Two of the samples tested positive for the bacteria.
examples.cn: 其中两份样本的细菌检测呈阳性。

examples.en: Try to frame the feedback in positive terms before listing the problems.
examples.cn: 在列举问题之前，尽量用正面措辞来组织反馈。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖则提夫”——把好处剖出来、提出来给大家看，就是 positive（积极的、正面的）

root: 拉丁语 ponere“放置”的过去分词 positus → positivus“经约定确定的” → 英语 positive（14 世纪，先用于法律与哲学）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is 'settled, laid down'. A settled answer is affirmative; settled evidence is proof; a settled direction on the axis is plus; a settled charge is positive; a settled outlook is optimism. The grammatical sense is simply the form before comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是“被确定、被定下”。确定下来的回答是肯定；确定下来的证据是确凿；轴上确定下来的方向是正；确定下来的电荷是正电；确定下来的看法是乐观。语法义则只是比较之前的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark placed firmly on the plus side of a line, with nothing left open.
core.cn: 核心意象：在一条线的正侧牢牢按下记号，不留任何悬而未决。

branches.en: CERTAINTY: the firm yes and the proof that closes the question.
branches.cn: 确定：干脆的“是”，以及关闭问题的证据。

branches.en: VALUE: the hopeful outlook and the good effect it expects.
branches.cn: 价值：乐观的心态，以及它所期待的良好效果。

branches.en: DIAGNOSIS: the test that finds the thing present.
branches.cn: 诊断：查出某物确实存在的检测。

branches.en: SIGN: the plus side of the number line and of the electric charge.
branches.cn: 符号：数轴与电荷的正侧。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the plain degree, stated before any comparison.
branches.cn: 语法：任何比较之前的朴素级。

intro.en: Positive is built from a Latin participle plus the adjective ending -ivus. The same stem, with different prefixes, yields most of the place-and-state vocabulary of English.
intro.cn: positive 由一个拉丁分词加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。同一个词干配上不同前缀，产出了英语里大量表示“放置与状态”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin positus is the pivot: every word below either contains it or is built by adding a prefix to the verb it comes from.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 positus 是枢纽：下面每个词要么含有它，要么是在其来源动词上加前缀构成。

items.meaning: tending toward, having the nature of
items.meaningCN: 倾向于；具有……性质的形容词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀
表示学说或体系的词尾

latinEntries.meaningCN: 经约定确定的；约定俗成的

definition_zh: 潜在的；可能的；有潜力的；（名词）潜力；电势；势能
definition_en: possible but not yet actual; having the capacity to develop into something; (noun) the capacity to become something in the future
core_image: 一枚还没拉开的弓：力已经存着，只是尚未射出
scene: 药房里，药剂师指着说明书上的警示行。She said: Potential side effects make this drug dangerous when it is taken with alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 potential 是「潜在的、可能发生但还没发生的」（第 1 个义项：以一种可能性的方式存在）；句意：潜在的副作用会让这种药与酒精同服时变得危险。场景要点：还没发生、但条件一凑就会发生。

pos.zh: 潜在的；可能的；有潜力的

derivatives.zh: 强有力的；有效的（同出 posse）
全能的（omni- 全部 + potens 有能力）

senses.title: Possible but not yet actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在的：可能发生，但还没发生
senses.definition: existing as a possibility rather than as a fact
senses.definitionCN: 以一种可能性的方式存在，而非作为事实存在
senses.example: The drug is potentially dangerous if taken with alcohol.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药如果与酒精同服，可能有危险。
senses.why: Latin posse means 'to be able'. Potential marks what is able to happen without having happened yet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 posse 意为“能够”。potential 标记的是“能够发生、但尚未发生”的东西。

senses.title: Having latent ability
senses.titleCN: 有潜力的：本事藏着，还没使出来
senses.definition: having an ability that is not yet developed or shown
senses.definitionCN: 拥有尚未发展或尚未显现的能力
senses.example: She is a potential national champion in the 800 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她有可能成为 800 米全国冠军。
senses.why: The same 'able to be' applies to a person: the capacity is real, the achievement is not yet.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“能够成为”用在人身上：能力是真实的，成就还没到。

senses.title: Physics: stored energy
senses.titleCN: 势能：存着还没放出来的能量
senses.definition: energy that a body has because of its position or condition, rather than because of motion
senses.definitionCN: 物体因位置或状态而具有的能量，而非因运动而具有的能量
senses.example: The water behind the dam has a great deal of potential energy.
senses.exampleCN: 坝后的水具有大量势能。
senses.why: Energy held in place is ability waiting to be released. Physics named it with the same word for capacity.
senses.whyCN: 被位置存住的能量，就是等着被释放的“能够”。物理学用了同一个表示“能力”的词来命名它。

senses.title: Physics: electric potential
senses.titleCN: 电势：电场里某点的“位势”
senses.definition: the amount of electric potential energy per unit charge at a point in a field
senses.definitionCN: 电场中某点单位电荷所具有的电势能
senses.example: Current flows from higher to lower electric potential.
senses.exampleCN: 电流从电势较高处流向电势较低处。
senses.why: A charge at a point in a field has stored ability to move. That stored ability, measured per charge, is the potential.
senses.whyCN: 电场中某点的电荷存有移动的能力。把这份储存的能力按单位电荷计量，就是电势。

senses.title: Grammar: expressing possibility
senses.titleCN: 语法：表示可能性的语气
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a mood or form that presents something as possible rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指把某事呈现为可能而非现实的形式或语气
senses.example: In some languages the potential mood marks what may happen.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言用可能语气标记可能发生的事。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the word to name the form whose job is exactly this: stating what can be, without stating that it is.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，来命名那种专门做这件事的形式：说出“可能是什么”，而不说“就是什么”。

senses.title: Noun: the possibility of something
senses.titleCN: 名词：某事发生的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility that something will happen or can be developed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或可以被发展出来的可能性
senses.example: The potential for conflict remains high in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区发生冲突的可能性仍然很高。
senses.why: The adjective's abstract quality becomes a noun: not a possible thing, but possibility itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词的抽象性质变成名词：不是某个可能之物，而是“可能性”本身。

senses.title: Noun: undeveloped capacity in a person
senses.titleCN: 名词：一个人身上尚未长成的本事
senses.definition: the capacity a person has to develop and succeed in the future
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在未来发展与取得成就的能力
senses.example: The coach saw potential in the young goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在这个年轻守门员身上看到了潜力。
senses.why: A person is treated like a body with stored energy: what is there now is less than what it can become.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成一个储能的身体：现在已有的，少于它将来能成为的。

senses.title: Physics: potential difference
senses.titleCN: 电势差：两点之间的位势落差
senses.definition: the difference in electric potential between two points, measured in volts
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间电势的差值，以伏特计
senses.example: A battery maintains a potential difference across its terminals.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在其两端维持一个电势差。
senses.why: Difference is what makes stored ability flow. The gap between two potentials is the push that moves charge.
senses.whyCN: 落差才使储存的能力流动。两个电势之间的差距，就是推动电荷移动的那股力。

intro.en: Potential comes from the Latin verb for being able. The idea is capacity that has not yet turned into act, which is why the word serves both for people and for stored energy.
intro.cn: potential 来自拉丁语中表示“能够”的动词。其观念是“尚未变成现实的能力”，所以它既可用于人，也可用于储存的能量。

items.en: Posse meant 'to be able, to have power'. It is a compound of potis 'able' plus esse 'to be', literally 'to be able'.
items.cn: posse 意为“能够、有力量”。它由 potis“有能力的”加 esse“存在、是”构成，字面即“能够是”。

items.en: The present participle potens meant 'being able, powerful'. English potent and omnipotent come from this form.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens 意为“有能力的、强大的”。英语 potent 与 omnipotent 来自这个形式。

items.en: Potentia meant 'power, ability, capacity'. It names the quality rather than the act, which is exactly the seed of the modern word.
items.cn: potentia 意为“力量、能力、潜能”。它命名的是性质而非行动，这正是现代这个词的种子。

items.en: Potentialis was formed from potentia plus -alis, meaning 'having power or capacity'. Medieval philosophy used it for what can exist without existing yet.
items.cn: potentialis 由 potentia 加 -alis 构成，意为“具有力量或能力的”。中世纪哲学用它指“能够存在但尚未存在”的东西。

items.en: English potential enters in the 17th century, first in philosophy and grammar. The scientific senses of potential energy and electric potential follow in the 19th century.
items.cn: 英语 potential 于 17 世纪进入，最早用于哲学与语法。势能与电势的科学义则在 19 世纪跟进。

items.en: Modern English uses it for latent ability in people, for possible risks and customers, and for the technical quantities named after stored energy.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指人身上尚未显现的能力、可能的风险与客户，以及那些以储存能量命名的技术量。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for being able. The second group collects words for what may happen and what is not yet developed.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“能够”的词根。第二组收表示“可能发生”与“尚未发展”的词。

entries.definition: possibly, in a way that may become real. It softens a claim: potentially dangerous means may be dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 可能地，以某种或将成真的方式。它使断言变软：potentially dangerous 意为“可能有危险”。

entries.definition: powerful or effective. Potent describes power already present; potential describes power not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 强有力的、有效的。potent 描述已经在场的力；potential 描述尚未使用的力。

entries.definition: the state of being possible or having latent capacity. It is the philosophical noun built on potential.
entries.definitionCN: 处于可能状态或具有潜在能力。它是建立在 potential 之上的哲学名词。

entries.definition: all-powerful. Omni- 'all' plus potens 'able': able to do everything.
entries.definitionCN: 全能的。omni-“全部”加 potens“有能力的”：能做一切。

entries.definition: able to happen or be true. Possible is wider; potential often suggests a capacity that can be developed.
entries.definitionCN: 能够发生或为真。possible 更宽；potential 常暗示一种可以被发展出来的能力。

entries.definition: present but not yet active or visible. Latent stresses hiddenness; potential stresses capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未活动或显现。latent 强调隐藏；potential 强调能力。

entries.definition: likely to happen or to become something in the future. Prospective is about the future position; potential is about the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 未来可能发生或成为的。prospective 关乎未来的位置；potential 关乎能力。

entries.definition: signs that someone or something will do well. Promise is the informal judgement; potential is the neutral capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某人或某物会出色的迹象。promise 是非正式的判断；potential 是中性的能力。

entries.definition: the amount something can hold or do. Capacity is measurable; potential can be unmeasured and unrealized.
entries.definitionCN: 某物能容纳或能做到的量。capacity 可测量；potential 可以未被测量、未被实现。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the drawn bow, the unseen champion, the water behind the dam, the battery terminal, and the coach's eye.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：拉开的弓、还没出头的冠军、坝后的水、电池两端、教练的眼光。

normal.en: Potential is a drawn bow: the force is already stored, only the release has not happened.
normal.cn: potential 是一张拉开的弓：力已经存好，只是还没放箭。

normal.en: A potential champion is someone whose trophy is still in the future.
normal.cn: a potential champion 是奖杯还在未来的人。

normal.en: Water held behind a dam is potential energy: high up, still, waiting.
normal.cn: 坝后存住的水就是势能：位置高、静止、等着。

normal.en: A battery keeps a potential difference: one terminal is higher than the other, and charge wants to flow down.
normal.cn: 电池维持电势差：一端比另一端高，电荷就想往下流。

normal.en: A coach sees potential, which means seeing the future player inside the present one.
normal.cn: 教练看到潜力，就是从现在这个球员身上看到未来的那个。

abstract.en: Potential is the gap between what is and what could be, and every measurement of it is a guess about the future.
abstract.cn: 潜力是“是什么”与“可能是什么”之间的落差，对它的每一次测量都是对未来的猜测。

abstract.en: Stored energy and undeveloped talent share one word because both are ability held in place.
abstract.cn: 储存的能量与未发展的才能共用一个词，因为两者都是被位置存住的“能够”。

abstract.en: Calling something potential is a way of praising it without yet committing to it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为 potential，是一种既赞美它、又尚未对它作出承诺的说法。

examples.en: The region has enormous potential for solar power.
examples.cn: 该地区在太阳能方面有巨大潜力。

examples.en: Investors were warned about the potential loss of their deposits.
examples.cn: 投资者被警告存款可能遭受损失。

examples.en: She never reached her full potential as a runner because of injuries.
examples.cn: 因为伤病，她从未跑出自己全部的潜力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破天秀”——还没出手就已经很秀，潜力（potential）藏在天分里

root: 拉丁语 posse“能够”（potis“有能力的”+ esse“是”）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“能力”→ 晚期拉丁 potentialis → 英语 potential（17 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Everything turns on the difference between able-to-be and being. A possible event, an undeveloped talent, stored energy, a voltage, and a grammatical mood all describe capacity before it becomes act.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都围绕“能够成为”与“已经成为”的差别。可能发生的事、未发展的才能、储存的能量、电压、语法语气，描述的都是“变成行动之前的能力”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched bow held still, force stored and not yet released.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉满却静持的弓，力已储存，尚未放出。

branches.en: POSSIBILITY: what may happen, stated as an adjective and as a noun.
branches.cn: 可能性：可能发生之事，分别用形容词与名词表达。

branches.en: TALENT: capacity inside a person, seen by a coach or by the person herself.
branches.cn: 才能：人身上的能力，被教练或本人看见。

branches.en: STORED ENERGY: the bow, the dam, the lifted weight.
branches.cn: 储能：弓、坝、被举高的重物。

branches.en: ELECTRICITY: the level at a point and the difference between two points.
branches.cn: 电学：某点的电势与两点之间的电势差。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the form whose whole job is to say 'may be'.
branches.cn: 语法：专门负责说“可能是”的那个形式。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for being able. Its participles and abstract nouns supply potent, potential, and potentiality; prefixes add scope such as all or many.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表示“能够”的动词上。它的分词与抽象名词提供了 potent、potential、potentiality；前缀则加上“全部”“多”等范围。

latinIntro.en: Latin potens and potentia passed into English through scientific and philosophical writing, so the technical senses retain their Latin shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potens 与 potentia 经科学与哲学写作进入英语，所以技术义仍保留拉丁形态。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 多能的（能分化成多种细胞）

definition_zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于；作为……的前身
definition_en: to come or go before something or someone in time, order, position, or rank
core_image: 一个人先一步走过路口，后面的人还没到
scene: A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 precede 是「在时间上先于」（第 1 个义项）；句意：颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。场景要点：先后顺序、前一件先发生、后一件才登场。

pos.zh: 先于；在……之前；走在前面；位次高于

senses.title: To happen earlier in time
senses.titleCN: 先于：在时间上更早发生
senses.definition: to happen or exist before something else in time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上比另一事物更早发生或存在
senses.example: A short speech preceded the award ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖典礼之前先有一段简短致辞。
senses.why: Latin praecedere is prae 'before' plus cedere 'go'. The first sense is simply going earlier along the timeline.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecedere 是 prae“在前”加 cedere“走”。第一个义项就是沿着时间线走得更早。

senses.title: To come earlier in an order
senses.titleCN: 排在前面：顺序上在前
senses.definition: to come before something else in a sequence, list, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在序列、清单或排列中位于另一事物之前
senses.example: The prefix precedes the root in this word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个词里，前缀排在词根之前。
senses.why: Time becomes sequence. What goes first on a line is what has preceded the rest, even when no clock is involved.
senses.whyCN: 时间变成了顺序。在一条线上排在最前的，就是先于其余各项的，即使不涉及钟表。

senses.title: To walk in front of
senses.titleCN: 走在前面：身体在前头
senses.definition: to go in front of someone, especially in a procession or on a route
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人前面，尤指在游行队伍或行进路线上
senses.example: A drummer preceded the bridal party down the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一名鼓手走在迎亲队伍前面，沿街而行。
senses.why: This is the literal picture of the Latin verb: one body moving ahead of another along the same road.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词最字面的画面：一具身体沿着同一条路走在另一具前面。

senses.title: To outrank or take priority
senses.titleCN: 优先：位次或重要性在前
senses.definition: to be higher in rank, importance, or priority than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在级别、重要性或优先次序上高于某人或某物
senses.example: In this court, federal law precedes state law.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个法庭上，联邦法优先于州法。
senses.why: A procession has an order of dignity as well as an order in space. Whoever goes first is served first, so position becomes priority.
senses.whyCN: 队伍不只有空间顺序，还有尊卑顺序。走在前面的人先被招待，于是位置变成了优先权。

senses.title: To go ahead as an introduction
senses.titleCN: 先行开道：把后面的引出来
senses.definition: to come before something as its introduction or preparation
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的引子或准备而出现在它之前
senses.example: A period of quiet preceded the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨之前有一段平静。
senses.why: What goes first can prepare the way for what follows. The earlier thing is not merely earlier; it ushers the later one in.
senses.whyCN: 走在前面的东西可以为后面的东西铺路。先前之物不只是更早，它还把后来者引了进来。

senses.title: To be the forerunner of
senses.titleCN: 是……的前身：更早的版本
senses.definition: to be an earlier form or ancestor of something that came later
senses.definitionCN: 是后来某事物的较早形态或前身
senses.example: The telegraph preceded the telephone by decades.
senses.exampleCN: 电报比电话早出现了几十年。
senses.why: Objects too can walk in a line through history. The older device stands in front of the newer one, which is its descendant.
senses.whyCN: 物件也能在历史中排队行走。较老的装置站在较新的前面，后者是它的后裔。

senses.title: To preface with words
senses.titleCN: 开场先说：用话在前面铺一层
senses.definition: to say something before the main statement or text
senses.definitionCN: 在主要陈述或正文之前先说一些话
senses.example: He preceded his refusal with a long apology.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拒绝之前先说了很长一段道歉。
senses.why: Speech has an order too. Words placed in front of the main message are doing the walking-ahead.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有顺序。放在主要信息前面的那些话，承担的就是“走在前面”的功能。

senses.title: Literary: to have gone before others
senses.titleCN: 书面：先走一步（指已故的先辈）
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, to have gone before others, especially to have died earlier
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，指先于他人离去，尤指更早去世
senses.example: We honor those who preceded us and built this town.
senses.exampleCN: 我们敬重那些先我们而去、建起这座小镇的人。
senses.why: A procession through life has a front and a back. Those already further along are described as having preceded the living.
senses.whyCN: 穿越一生的队伍有前有后。已经走得更远的人，就被说成先于在世者而行。

intro.en: Precede is a transparent Latin compound: before plus go. Nearly all of its English senses are versions of that one physical picture.
intro.cn: precede 是一个构造透明的拉丁复合词：“在前”加“走”。它在英语里的几乎每个义项，都是这一幅身体画面的变体。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front of'. It is the source of the English prefix pre-, and it marks position in space as well as priority in time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前、在……之前”。它是英语前缀 pre- 的来源，既标记空间位置，也标记时间上的优先。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to yield, to withdraw'. English gets cede, accede, exceed, proceed, and succeed from this verb.
items.cn: cedere 意为“走、让、退”。英语的 cede、accede、exceed、proceed、succeed 都出自这个动词。

items.en: Praecedere meant 'to go before, to precede'. It described both people walking ahead and events coming earlier.
items.cn: praecedere 意为“走在前面、先于”。它既描述人走在前头，也描述事件更早发生。

items.en: Old French took the verb as preceder, keeping the sense of going or coming before.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词接作 preceder，保留“走在前面、先来”的意思。

items.en: English precede is recorded in the 15th century. The legal noun precedent and the noun precedence grow from the same root.
items.cn: 英语 precede 记录于 15 世纪。法律名词 precedent 与名词 precedence 都从同一个词根长出。

items.en: Modern usage extends the image to ranks, arguments, inventions, and even the dead: whatever stands earlier in a line has preceded what stands later.
items.cn: 现代用法把这幅画面扩展到等级、论证、发明，甚至逝者：凡在一条线上站得更早的，就先于站得更晚的。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for going. The second group collects words for coming before in time, order, and rank.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“走”的动词。第二组收表示“在时间、顺序、等级上在前”的词。

entries.definition: to go forward or continue. Pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'go', so it moves ahead rather than before.
entries.definitionCN: 前进或继续进行。pro-“向前”加 cedere“走”，所以它是向前走，而非走在前面。

entries.definition: an earlier case used as a rule for later ones. It is the noun of precede in legal usage.
entries.definitionCN: 被用作后来案例规则的先前判例。它是 precede 在法律用法中的名词。

entries.definition: the person who held a post before another. From Latin prae- plus decedere 'to go away', literally one who went before.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人之前担任某职位的人。来自拉丁 prae- 加 decedere“离开”，字面即“先走的人”。

entries.definition: the right to go or be treated first. It is the abstract noun of precede.
entries.definitionCN: 先行或被优先对待的权利。它是 precede 的抽象名词。

entries.definition: to exist or happen before something in date. Predate is narrower, used only of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在日期上早于某事物。predate 更窄，只用于时间。

entries.definition: to be earlier than, or to put an earlier date on. Antedate is formal and often about documents.
entries.definitionCN: 早于，或在文件上写较早的日期。antedate 较正式，常用于文件。

entries.definition: to go in front and show the way. Lead implies guiding; precede only states the order.
entries.definitionCN: 走在前面并带路。lead 含引导之意；precede 只陈述先后顺序。

entries.definition: to have a higher rank than someone. Outrank matches sense 04 exactly and is used of people and offices.
entries.definitionCN: 级别高于某人。outrank 精确对应第 4 义项，多用于人与职位。

entries.definition: to go before as a sign or precursor. Forerun is literary and rare; its noun forerunner is common.
entries.definitionCN: 作为征兆或先驱先行。forerun 带文学色彩且少见；其名词 forerunner 更常用。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the walker ahead, the prefix before the root, the court that hears federal law first, the older machine, and the ancestors.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：走在前面的人、词根前的前缀、先审联邦法的法庭、更老的机器、先辈。

normal.en: Pre- means before, cede means go. Precede is literally before-go.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，cede 是“走”。precede 字面就是“先走”。

normal.en: In the word unhappy, un- precedes happy: it walks in front of the root.
normal.cn: 在 unhappy 这个词里，un- 走在 happy 前面，就是 precede 词根。

normal.en: Take precedence: whoever walks first gets served first.
normal.cn: take precedence：谁走在前面，谁先被招待。

normal.en: The telegraph preceded the telephone; the older machine stands in front of the newer one in history's queue.
normal.cn: 电报先于电话；在历史的队伍里，更老的机器站在更新的前面。

normal.en: Those who preceded us are the ones already further up the road.
normal.cn: 先我们而去的人，就是已经在路上走得更远的那些。

abstract.en: Order is not a thing in the world but a line we draw; precede is the word for standing on the earlier side of that line.
abstract.cn: 顺序不是世界里的物件，而是我们画的线；precede 就是在一条线较早一侧站着的说法。

abstract.en: Priority borrows its grammar from walking: we say law comes first as if laws had legs.
abstract.cn: 优先权借用了行走的语法：我们说法律“在先”，仿佛法律长了腿。

abstract.en: Every forerunner is only recognized as one after the thing it preceded has arrived.
abstract.cn: 每一个前身，都只有在它所先行的那件事到来之后，才被认出来是前身。

examples.en: The years preceding the war were marked by rapid industrial growth.
examples.cn: 战前那些年以快速的工业增长为标志。

examples.en: In the protocol, the chair's remarks precede the vote.
examples.cn: 按议程，主席发言在投票之前。

examples.en: Several small tremors preceded the main earthquake.
examples.cn: 主震之前发生了数次小震动。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞西德”——普瑞先一步西德而行，就是 precede（先于、走在前面）

root: 拉丁语 praecedere＝prae“在前”+ cedere“走” → 古法语 preceder → 英语 precede（15 世纪）；与 proceed、precedent、predecessor、cede 同根。

sensesIntro.en: One physical image serves everything: something moves ahead of something else on the same line. Time, sequence, space, rank, introduction, ancestry, and even death are all lines along which one item can stand before another.
sensesIntro.cn: 一幅身体画面统摄全部义项：某物在同一条线上走在另一物前面。时间、顺序、空间、等级、引子、前身，甚至死亡，都是可以让一个项目站在另一个之前的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker a few steps ahead of another on the same road.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路上，一个行者比另一个领先几步。

branches.en: TIME AND SEQUENCE: earlier on the timeline or in the list.
branches.cn: 时间与顺序：在时间线上或清单里更早。

branches.en: SPACE: a body moving in front along a route.
branches.cn: 空间：一具身体沿路线走在前面。

branches.en: RANK: position turned into priority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：位置变成优先权与位次。

branches.en: INTRODUCTION: what goes first to prepare or frame what follows.
branches.cn: 引子：先走一步，为后面的东西铺路或定框。

branches.en: LINEAGE: the earlier device and the people already further along.
branches.cn: 谱系：更早的器物，以及已经走得更远的人。

intro.en: Precede is built from a prefix of position and a verb of motion. The same two pieces, with other prefixes, produce much of the vocabulary of going and yielding.
intro.cn: precede 由一个表位置的前缀和一个表运动的动词构成。同样两个构件配上别的前缀，产出了大量表示“行走与让渡”的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecedere passed into French and English; its participle and noun forms supplied precedent, precedence, and predecessor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecedere 传入法语与英语；它的分词与名词形式提供了 precedent、precedence、predecessor。

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者或性质的后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的；恰好的
definition_en: exact and accurate in detail; clearly defined and not approximate; careful about details
core_image: 一刀切下去，边缘干净，不多不少
scene: The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
sceneCN: 这里 precise 是「精确到很小单位」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。场景要点：刻度细、读数明确、没有模糊区间。

pos.zh: 精确的；准确的；明确的；严谨的

senses.title: Exact in measurement
senses.titleCN: 精确的：读数细到很小一格
senses.definition: exact and accurate, with details measured or stated to a fine degree
senses.definitionCN: 精确而准确，细节被测量或陈述到很细的程度
senses.example: The instrument can measure temperature to a precise tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能把温度测量到十分之一度的精确度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere means to cut off. A precise measurement is one cut cleanly, with no ragged margin of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecidere 意为“切掉”。精确的测量就是切得干净，边缘没有参差的疑问。

senses.title: Clearly defined and distinct
senses.titleCN: 明确的：边界画得清
senses.definition: clearly stated or defined, so that there is no ambiguity
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或界定清楚，因而没有歧义
senses.example: The contract gives a precise definition of the delivery date.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对交付日期给出了明确的定义。
senses.why: If the edges are cut cleanly, the shape is unambiguous. A precise definition has no fuzzy border where other things could slip in.
senses.whyCN: 边缘切得干净，形状就不含糊。明确的定义没有模糊的边界，别的东西无从混入。

senses.title: Careful about small details
senses.titleCN: 严谨的：在小处也不放过
senses.definition: careful and exact in doing or describing something, paying attention to small details
senses.definitionCN: 在做或描述某事时仔细准确，注意细小之处
senses.example: She is precise about the order of the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 她对步骤的先后十分严谨。
senses.why: The cut-clean image becomes a habit of mind: refusing to let any detail stay rough.
senses.whyCN: “切得干净”的画面变成一种思维习惯：不允许任何细节保持粗糙。

senses.title: Strict about rules or standards
senses.titleCN: 讲究的：按规矩来，不将就
senses.definition: strict and particular about how things are done, often in matters of form
senses.definitionCN: 对做事方式严格挑剔，常指形式与礼数方面
senses.example: He was precise in his dress and punctual to the minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他衣着讲究，并且准时到分钟。
senses.why: A person who cuts every edge cleanly can become a person who insists on exact form. The trait shifts from result to temperament.
senses.whyCN: 一个把每条边都切干净的人，可能变成坚持确切形式的人。这个特征从结果转到了性情。

senses.title: Emphatic: the very same
senses.titleCN: 恰好的：正是那一个
senses.definition: used to emphasize that a particular thing or moment is exactly the one meant
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调所说的正是那一个事物或那一刻
senses.example: At that precise moment, the lights went out.
senses.exampleCN: 正是在那一刻，灯灭了。
senses.why: An exact point has no width. Using precise here says the moment cannot be widened into a general period.
senses.whyCN: 一个精确的点没有宽度。这里用 precise，是说那一刻无法被放宽成一段笼统的时期。

senses.title: Technical: high precision
senses.titleCN: 精密的：仪器能做到极细刻度
senses.definition: of an instrument or method, able to produce very exact results
senses.definitionCN: 指仪器或方法能给出非常精确的结果
senses.example: Precise instruments are required for this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验需要精密的仪器。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the tool that makes the clean cut. Precision becomes a property of the instrument, not only of the number.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词贴到了做出干净切割的工具上。精确性成了仪器的属性，而不只是数字的属性。

senses.title: Discourse: to be exact
senses.titleCN: 话语：确切地说
senses.definition: in the phrase to be precise, used to correct or narrow what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 在 to be precise 这一短语中，用来修正或收窄刚才说过的话
senses.example: He arrived late, at ten past eight, to be precise.
senses.exampleCN: 他到得晚了，确切地说是八点十分。
senses.why: The speaker performs the cutting in speech: trimming a rough statement down to its exact edge.
senses.whyCN: 说话人在言语里执行这一刀：把粗略的说法修到确切的边缘。

senses.title: Neatly executed in movement or art
senses.titleCN: 动作精准：每一笔每一动都不含糊
senses.definition: performed with exact control, as in dance, surgery, or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 以精确的控制完成，如舞蹈、手术或绘画中的动作
senses.example: The dancer's precise movements made the whole phrase look effortless.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者精准的动作让整个乐句显得毫不费力。
senses.why: The body can cut cleanly too. Precision in movement is the same refusal of slack, expressed in muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体也能切得干净。动作的精准是同一种对松弛的拒绝，只是用肌肉表达出来。

intro.en: Precise comes from a Latin participle meaning cut off. The path from 'cut short' to 'exact' is the story of a metaphor that became a standard.
intro.cn: precise 来自一个意为“被切掉”的拉丁分词。从“切短”到“精确”的路径，是一个比喻变成标准的历程。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Here it intensifies rather than marks time: the cutting is done right at the front edge.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。这里它起加强作用而非标时间：这一刀正切在前沿上。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike'. English gets scissors, decide, concise, and circumcise from this family.
items.cn: caedere 意为“切、砍”。英语的 scissors、decide、concise、circumcise 都出自这个词族。

items.en: Praecidere meant 'to cut off, to cut short'. It described trimming something down to a clean limit.
items.cn: praecidere 意为“切掉、切短”。它描述把某物修到干净的界限。

items.en: The past participle praecisus meant 'cut off, shortened'. It is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 praecisus 意为“被切掉的、被缩短的”。它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: French used précis for 'cut short, concise, exact'. English borrowed the form in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语用 précis 表示“切短的、简洁的、确切的”。英语在 16 世纪借入这个词形。

items.en: The sense moves from 'cut short' to 'definite' and then to 'accurate to a fine degree'. Modern usage applies it to numbers, definitions, instruments, people, and moments.
items.cn: 词义从“切短”转到“确定”，再转到“精确到很细的程度”。现代用法把它用于数字、定义、仪器、人以及时刻。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for cutting. The second group collects words for accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“切”的动词。第二组收表示准确与确切的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being exact, or the degree of exactness. It is the noun built on precise.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，或精确的程度。它是建立在 precise 之上的名词。

entries.definition: exactly, or used to confirm a statement. Precisely can answer a question with a firm yes.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，或用于确认某陈述。precisely 可以以干脆的“正是”来回答提问。

entries.definition: brief and clear. Con- 'together' plus caedere 'cut': cut down to essentials.
entries.definitionCN: 简短而清楚。con-“一起”加 caedere“切”：切到只剩要点。

entries.definition: to settle a question. De- 'off' plus caedere 'cut': cut off alternatives until one remains.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题定下来。de-“去掉”加 caedere“切”：切掉其他选项，直到只剩一个。

entries.definition: correct in every detail. Exact stresses correctness; precise stresses fine definition and care.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都正确。exact 强调正确；precise 强调界定细密与讲究。

entries.definition: correct and free from error. Accurate is about truth to fact; precise is about narrowness of specification.
entries.definitionCN: 正确且无错误。accurate 关乎与事实相符；precise 关乎规格的窄细。

entries.definition: clearly identified rather than general. Specific names the thing; precise describes how finely it is defined.
entries.definitionCN: 明确指出的，而非笼统的。specific 指名的是哪一个；precise 描述界定得多细。

entries.definition: showing great attention to detail. Meticulous fits sense 03 and stresses care rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 对细节极为注意。meticulous 对应第 3 义项，强调用心而非测量。

entries.definition: clear and not uncertain. Definite fits sense 02 and is close to the 'cut clean' image.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不含糊。definite 对应第 2 义项，贴近“切得干净”的画面。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the clean cut, the narrow definition, the meticulous person, the exact instant, and the phrase to be precise.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：干净的一刀、窄而清楚的定义、一丝不苟的人、正好的那一刻、以及 to be precise 这句话。

normal.en: Precise comes from a verb meaning to cut off. Picture a knife trimming away every loose edge.
normal.cn: precise 来自意为“切掉”的动词。想象一把刀把每一条松散的边都修掉。

normal.en: A precise definition has a clean border: nothing else can slip in.
normal.cn: 明确的定义有一条干净的边界：别的东西混不进来。

normal.en: Precise instruments are the ones whose readings do not wobble.
normal.cn: 精密的仪器，就是读数不会晃的那种。

normal.en: At that precise moment means the moment has no width; you cannot widen it into an afternoon.
normal.cn: at that precise moment 意为那一刻没有宽度，你不能把它放宽成一个下午。

normal.en: To be precise is to take the rough sentence and trim it to its exact edge.
normal.cn: to be precise 就是把粗糙的句子修到确切的边缘。

abstract.en: Precision is a relation between a statement and a tolerance, not a property of the world by itself.
abstract.cn: 精确是陈述与容许误差之间的关系，不是世界本身的属性。

abstract.en: Every precise definition is also an exclusion: to say exactly what it is, is to say what it is not.
abstract.cn: 每个明确的定义同时也是一次排除：说清它是什么，就是说清它不是什么。

abstract.en: The same cut that makes a thing exact can make it narrow; precision always trades scope for edge.
abstract.cn: 使事物精确的那一刀，也可能使它变窄；精确总是用范围换取边缘。

examples.en: The instructions were precise enough that a beginner could follow them.
examples.cn: 这些指示足够精确，初学者也能照着做。

examples.en: To be precise, the meeting lasted forty-two minutes.
examples.cn: 确切地说，会议持续了四十二分钟。

examples.en: Her precise handwriting filled the margins without a single correction.
examples.cn: 她精准的字迹填满了页边，没有一处涂改。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞赛斯”——普瑞在赛前把秒表按到千分之一秒，就是 precise（精确的）

root: 拉丁语 praecidere“切掉、切短”（prae“在前”+ caedere“切”）的过去分词 praecisus → 法语 précis → 英语 precise（16 世纪）；与 concise、decide、scissors 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clean cut. A clean cut gives exact numbers, unambiguous definitions, meticulous habits, and instruments that do not wobble. The emphatic use fixes one instant, and to be precise performs the same trimming in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是干净的一刀。干净的一刀给出精确的数字、不含糊的定义、一丝不苟的习惯，以及不晃的仪器。强调用法固定住某一刻，而 to be precise 是在言语里执行同一番修边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade trimming an edge until nothing rough is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃修边，直到不剩一点毛糙。

branches.en: MEASURE: exact readings and the instruments that produce them.
branches.cn: 测量：精确的读数，以及产生这些读数的仪器。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: a definition with a clean edge, and a moment with no width.
branches.cn: 边界：边缘干净的定义，以及没有宽度的时刻。

branches.en: TEMPERAMENT: the meticulous person and the person strict about form.
branches.cn: 性情：一丝不苟的人，以及讲究形式的人。

branches.en: SPEECH: trimming a rough statement down to the exact word.
branches.cn: 言语：把粗略的说法修到确切的字眼。

branches.en: MOVEMENT: the same clean edge performed by the body.
branches.cn: 动作：由身体执行的同一种干净边缘。

intro.en: Precise is one participle from the cut family. The same verb, with different prefixes, gives concise, decide, and scissors.
intro.cn: precise 是“切”词族里的一个分词。同一个动词配上不同前缀，给出 concise、decide、scissors。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecisus reached English through French précis, which is why the English form lacks the Latin -us ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praecisus 经法语 précis 到达英语，所以英语形式没有拉丁的 -us 词尾。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料；预示
definition_en: to say or state in advance that something will happen, especially on the basis of evidence or reasoning
core_image: 站在今天，用话把明天的那件事先说出来
scene: Economists predict slower growth next year.
sceneCN: 这里 predict 是「依据数据对将来作出判断」（第 2 个义项：预测）；句意：经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。场景要点：用现有信息、指向未来、可被检验。

derivatives.zh: 不可预测的；变化莫测的

senses.title: To say what will happen
senses.titleCN: 预测：先说将来会发生什么
senses.definition: to state in advance that a particular event will happen
senses.definitionCN: 事先说明某个特定事件将会发生
senses.example: No one could predict which team would win.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预测哪支队伍会赢。
senses.why: Latin praedicere is prae 'before' plus dicere 'say'. The plain sense is saying something before it becomes true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praedicere 是 prae“在前”加 dicere“说”。最朴素的意思，就是在事情成真之前先把它说出来。

senses.title: To forecast from evidence
senses.titleCN: 预测：拿现有信息推算未来
senses.definition: to estimate a future state on the basis of data, models, or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或推理估计未来的状况
senses.example: Economists predict slower growth next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。
senses.why: The saying is not a guess but a calculation. Evidence is fed in, and the statement about the future comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这话不是猜的，而是算的。把证据喂进去，关于未来的陈述就出来了。

senses.title: Scientific prediction
senses.titleCN: 科学预言：理论先说出可检验的结果
senses.definition: to derive a testable consequence from a scientific theory before it is observed
senses.definitionCN: 在观察之前，从科学理论推出一个可检验的结果
senses.example: The theory predicted a new particle, which was found years later.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言了一种新粒子，数年后被找到。
senses.why: A good theory must be able to say what will be seen. Prediction is the test that separates science from speculation.
senses.whyCN: 好的理论必须能说出将会看到什么。预测是把科学与空想分开的那场考试。

senses.title: To indicate in advance by signs
senses.titleCN: 预示：迹象先替将来开口
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen, without anyone saying it in words
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将会发生的迹象，而非由人用话说出
senses.example: Dark clouds predicted a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: Signs can speak. When the world itself shows what is coming, we extend the verb from the speaker to the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象也能说话。当世界本身显露出即将发生的事，我们就把这个动词从说话者扩展到证据上。

senses.title: To prophesy
senses.titleCN: 预言：以先知的口吻宣告
senses.definition: to foretell future events as a prophet or oracle does, often without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或神谕那样预告未来，常无证据支持
senses.example: The old woman predicted that the drought would last seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人预言旱情会持续七年。
senses.why: The same act of speaking first, but the authority comes from revelation rather than from data.
senses.whyCN: 同样是先说出口的动作，只是权威来自启示而非数据。

senses.title: To expect or anticipate
senses.titleCN: 预料：心里已经先把它算上
senses.definition: to expect something to happen, often in everyday planning
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生，常用于日常安排
senses.example: We predicted heavy traffic and left an hour early.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料会堵车，所以提前一小时出发。
senses.why: Prediction need not be public. Private anticipation is the same forward-looking move, kept inside the head.
senses.whyCN: 预测不必公开。私下的预料是同一个朝前的动作，只是留在脑子里。

senses.title: Statistics: to estimate a value
senses.titleCN: 统计：给出一个估计值
senses.definition: to produce an estimated value for a future or unknown observation from a model
senses.definitionCN: 用模型为未来或未知的观测给出一个估计值
senses.example: The model predicts sales of 12,000 units in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测第一季度销量为一万二千件。
senses.why: In statistics the prediction is a number with an interval, not a sentence. The verb becomes a technical operation.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学里，预测是一个带区间的数，而不是一句话。这个动词变成了一项技术操作。

senses.title: To warn in advance
senses.titleCN: 预告：提前提醒，好让人准备
senses.definition: to announce something in advance so that people can prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 事先告知某事，以便人们可以准备
senses.example: The report predicted shortages and urged hospitals to stock up.
senses.exampleCN: 报告预告了短缺，并敦促医院囤货。
senses.why: Saying it early has a use: it buys time. Prediction becomes a warning when the future it names is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 提前说出来是有用的：它买来时间。当所命名的未来不受欢迎时，预测就成了预警。

intro.en: Predict is a Latin compound meaning to say beforehand. It is one of a large family built on the verb dicere, to say.
intro.cn: predict 是一个意为“事先说出”的拉丁复合词。它属于一个建立在动词 dicere（说）之上的大词族。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. It is the source of diction, dictionary, verdict, contradict, and predict.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、宣告”。它是 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict、predict 的来源。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Joined to a verb of saying, it produces the sense of saying something before its time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。与表示“说”的动词结合，就产生“在时间之前说出来”的意思。

items.en: Praedicere meant 'to make known beforehand, to declare in advance'. It was used for foretelling as well as for public proclamation.
items.cn: praedicere 意为“事先让人知道、预先宣告”。它既用于预言，也用于公开宣布。

items.en: The past participle praedictus meant 'foretold'. English keeps it inside words like prediction and predictably.
items.cn: 过去分词 praedictus 意为“被预言的”。英语把它保留在 prediction、predictably 这类词里。

items.en: English predict appears in the 16th century, at first in religious and learned writing about foretelling. The modern data-based sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语 predict 出现于 16 世纪，最早见于谈论预言的宗教与学术写作。以数据为基础的现代义要晚得多才发展出来。

items.en: With the rise of science and statistics, predict becomes the standard word for evidence-based foretelling, while prophesy remains the religious term.
items.cn: 随着科学与统计的兴起，predict 成了“有据预告”的标准词，而 prophesy 保持宗教色彩。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for saying. The second group collects words for foretelling, each with a different basis of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“说”的动词。第二组收表示“预告”的词，各自依据的权威不同。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It is the noun built on predict with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将会发生什么的陈述。它是 predict 加 -ion 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen, often with a hint of dullness. Predict plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被预见的，常带一点乏味的暗示。predict 加 -able。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject, or to base something on. It comes from Latin praedicare, a cousin of praedicere.
entries.definitionCN: 句子中陈述主语的部分，或“以……为依据”。它来自拉丁 praedicare，是 praedicere 的近亲。

entries.definition: a decision or judgement. Ver- 'true' plus dict 'said': what is said as true.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判定。ver-“真”加 dict“说”：被说成真实的话。

entries.definition: to say what is likely in weather, economics, or other systems. Forecast is common for weather and trends; predict is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 预告天气、经济或其他系统的可能状况。forecast 多用于天气与趋势；predict 是一般用语。

entries.definition: to tell of a future event. Foretell is literary and often implies a sign or a seer.
entries.definitionCN: 讲述未来的事件。foretell 带文学色彩，常暗示有征兆或预言者。

entries.definition: to foretell under divine inspiration. Prophesy claims a religious authority that predict does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在神圣启示下预告未来。prophesy 主张一种宗教权威，predict 没有这种主张。

entries.definition: to expect something and often act in advance. Anticipate adds preparation; predict can be purely a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 预期某事并常提前行动。anticipate 多出“准备”之意；predict 可以只是陈述。

entries.definition: to estimate future figures from present trends. Project is technical and numerical, closer to sense 07.
entries.definitionCN: 由当前趋势估算未来数字。project 是技术性、数值性的，更接近第 7 义项。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the sentence said too early, the economist's model, the particle found later, the dark clouds, and the shopping list made before the rush.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：提早说出的那句话、经济学家的模型、后来找到的粒子、乌云、以及抢购前先列好的清单。

normal.en: Pre- means before, dict means say. Predict is say-before.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，dict 是“说”。predict 就是“先说”。

normal.en: A weather forecast and a stock forecast are both predict with numbers plugged in.
normal.cn: 天气预报和股市预测，都是把数字代进去的 predict。

normal.en: A theory predicts a particle, then the lab goes looking for it. Prediction is the theory's exam.
normal.cn: 理论预言一种粒子，实验室随后去找它。预测就是理论的那场考试。

normal.en: Dark clouds predict rain without saying a word: signs can also speak.
normal.cn: 乌云一言不发就预示下雨：迹象也会说话。

normal.en: Predicting a rush and leaving early is the same verb, just kept private.
normal.cn: 预料拥堵并提早出门，是同一个动词，只是留在心里。

abstract.en: Every prediction is a promise the present makes about the future, and it can be broken by a single unforeseen event.
abstract.cn: 每个预测都是现在对未来作出的承诺，而它可能被一个未预见的事件打破。

abstract.en: The difference between prophecy and prediction is not the content but the warrant: revelation versus evidence.
abstract.cn: 预言与预测的差别不在内容，而在凭据：是启示，还是证据。

abstract.en: To predict well is to be willing to be wrong in public, which is why science prizes it.
abstract.cn: 预测得好，意味着愿意在公众面前出错；正因如此，科学看重它。

examples.en: The model predicts that sea levels will rise by about half a metre this century.
examples.cn: 该模型预测本世纪海平面将上升约半米。

examples.en: As predicted, the first frost came in the last week of October.
examples.cn: 正如所料，初霜在十月最后一周到来。

examples.en: Analysts predict a sharp fall in demand for new cars.
examples.cn: 分析人士预测新车需求将大幅下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞迪克特”——普瑞提前把“迪克特”那件事说出口，就是 predict（预测）

root: 拉丁语 praedicere“事先说出、预先宣告”＝prae“在前”+ dicere“说” → 英语 predict（16 世纪）；与 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means saying something before it happens. What changes is the basis: evidence, theory, signs, revelation, private expectation, or a statistical model. Each basis gives a slightly different shade of the same forward-speaking act.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“在事情发生之前先说出来”。变化的是依据：证据、理论、征兆、启示、私下预期，或统计模型。每一种依据都给同一个“朝前说话”的动作一种不同的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence spoken today about an event that has not yet arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天说出一句话，说的是尚未到来的事件。

branches.en: SPEECH: saying or expecting, public or private.
branches.cn: 言语：说出或预料，公开或私下。

branches.en: CALCULATION: forecasts from data, and statistical estimates.
branches.cn: 计算：由数据作出的预报，以及统计估计。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the theory that names a result before it is observed.
branches.cn: 科学：在结果被观察之前就把它命名的理论。

branches.en: SIGN AND WARNING: the world speaking through evidence, and the early notice that buys time.
branches.cn: 征兆与预警：世界借证据说话，以及买来时间的提前告知。

branches.en: PROPHECY: the same act, warranted by revelation.
branches.cn: 预言：同一个动作，凭据是启示。

intro.en: Predict is one compound from the large dicere family. Every word below is either a piece of that compound or a sibling built with another prefix on the same verb of saying.
intro.cn: predict 是 dicere 大词族里的一个复合词。下面每个词，要么是这个复合词的构件，要么是在同一个“说”的动词上加别的前缀构成的兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedicere and its participle praedictus supplied the English forms; the same dic- stem appears across law, grammar, and everyday speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praedicere 及其分词 praedictus 提供了英语形式；同一个 dic- 词干出现在法律、语法与日常言语中。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
